{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Development Strategy (strategy, revision 4 by Product Analyst, 8,963 characters)
Apple's strategy is to keep platform control and cash returns while buying the AI capability it did not build, which works financially but leaves the next upgrade cycle dependent on hardware mix, services growth and a competitor's model. In the first nine months of FY2026 Apple spent $34.04bn on research and development (+33%), $6.80bn on property, plant and equipment (down from $9.47bn) and $62.1bn buying back its own shares, while services grew 14% to $91.73bn at a 76.3% gross margin. The allocation is unambiguous: the balance sheet funds shareholders, the income statement funds AI. [S6]

### Capital returns come before capital projects

FY2025 set the pattern — $89.3bn of buybacks, $15.4bn of dividends, a new $100bn authorisation announced in May 2025 and a quarterly dividend raised to $0.26, against $34.55bn of R&D, up 10%. R&D is now growing three times faster than that, yet none of the increase goes into owned infrastructure. Returning cash while renting intelligence keeps return on equity high and removes the risk of stranded datacentres, but it also means Apple has no AI asset that a competitor cannot rent on similar terms. If features fail to lift average selling price, the R&D step-up is a pure margin cost, and the buyback is what keeps earnings per share intact. The investor gets a capital-return story with an AI expense line, not an AI investment cycle. [S5]

### Tariff insurance is being bought with margin

Apple assembled 55 million iPhones in India in 2025, up from 36 million, taking India to 25% of the 220-230 million made globally; Foxconn, Tata Electronics and Pegatron now build every iPhone 17 model there, including the Pro and Pro Max. The strategy is insurance against tariffs and China concentration, and it is working on volume. It is not free: assembly and components still cost more in India than in China or Vietnam, and smartphone production subsidies expired on 2026-03-31, with Apple and peers lobbying New Delhi for a further round. India is also becoming a demand market — sales above $9bn, six stores and Apple Pay planned for 2026. The hedge is real; the margin benefit is not yet. [S115]

### Services funds the strategy; regulation taxes it

Services is the profit engine, and its growth is concentrated where regulation bites: advertising and cloud services drove the 14% increase in the nine months to 2026-06-27, at a gross margin 1.5 times the company average. The Digital Markets Act makes that position contestable. By 2026-03-22 Apple had received 56 interoperability requests under Article 6(7), closing 43 of them and keeping 27 closures confidential, while continuing to challenge the obligations. Each request is engineering time and a potential loss of default status, the mechanism by which services margins are defended. Apple's response has been to comply narrowly and litigate broadly. [S6, S119]

### The AI layer is a partnership, not a programme

The defining strategic choice of the cycle was made on 2026-01-12, when Google confirmed a multi-year deal to supply Gemini models for the rebuilt Siri, reported at a 1.2-trillion-parameter model and $1bn a year. Apple paired that with rented Google TPU capacity for its own foundation models rather than building training clusters. The logic is defensible: ship a competitive assistant on time, keep the interface, personal context and the Private Cloud Compute boundary, and let a rival absorb frontier training costs. The price is strategic: the supplier also owns Android, and Apple's own research, while still credible, sits behind a rented frontier. Platform control is preserved at the layer users see; it is ceded at the layer that determines capability. The agreement was confirmed under Tim Cook, who moved to Executive Chairman on 2026-09-01 when John Ternus became chief executive, so execution now sits with Ternus and Federighi's software organisation rather than the negotiators: the contract is continuous, the signatory is not. A supplier that also owns Android has seen Apple slip once, which makes renewal terms the thing to watch — a licence priced per device or per query turns the AI bill into a services-margin item rather than an R&D line. [S111, S98]

| Partner | Scope | Signed or dated | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Google (Alphabet) | Gemini models for the rebuilt Siri, multi-year | 2026-01-12 | Confirmed by Google | S111 |
| Google Cloud | TPU training capacity for Apple foundation models | 2024, disclosed in Apple's model paper | In use | S118 |
| Foxconn, Tata Electronics, Pegatron | India assembly of the full iPhone line | Ongoing; 55 million units in 2025 | Operating | S115 |
| Klarna | Apple Upgrade device leasing in the U.S. | 2026, with iPhone 18 | Launched | S113 |

### The talent question is the weak link

The partnership was necessary partly because the in-house programme lost people: through 2025 Apple's AI executives and researchers left, mostly for Meta, which paid to recruit them. The leadership answer is now dated: on 2025-12-01 John Giannandrea, senior vice president for Machine Learning and AI Strategy, stepped down ahead of retirement, Amar Subramanya joined as vice president of AI, and Foundation Models, ML research and AI Safety and Evaluation moved into Software Engineering under Craig Federighi, with the rest going to Sabih Khan and Eddy Cue. Headcount-related expense is one of the two drivers Apple cites for the R&D increase, so the company is paying more for a team that is smaller at the top than it was two years ago. Apple still publishes competitive inference research, which argues against the strongest version of the decline story, but a research organisation folded into a software group while its flagship assistant runs on a licensed model is a programme in transition, not a moat under construction. [S121, S127]

### Second curves: health and foldables are adjacencies; Vision is not yet one

Health is the most defensible adjacency because it is regulated and sticky: hypertension notifications on Apple Watch carry FDA clearance and peer-reviewed scrutiny, giving owners a reason to upgrade and not to leave. The foldable Duo is the other extension, priced above the Pro Max and manufactured with a hinge that depends on AI-matched assembly and 3D printing rather than on scale alone. Vision Pro has no disclosed revenue, sits inside Wearables and has no confirmed successor: a research option, not a growth curve. The test of an adjacency is whether it earns its capital; health and foldables plausibly do, and the headset does not yet.

### What the next twelve months must prove

| Milestone | Target date | Status | What it proves | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FY2026 fourth-quarter results, guided to 9-11% revenue growth | 2026-11-02 | Scheduled | Whether iPhone 18 and Duo demand held through launch | S116 |
| Siri AI out of beta, with five more languages | From 2026-10 | Beta in English since 2026-09-14 | That a licensed model can be made to feel like an Apple product | S113 |
| Standard iPhone 18, 18e and Air 2 | Spring 2027, reported | Unlaunched | A two-cycle year and 2nm volume | S112 |
| Duo durability and return data | FY2027 | Not disclosed | Whether the foldable is a franchise or a flagship experiment | S114 |
| Renewal of India production incentives | After the 2026-03-31 expiry | Unresolved in the sources reviewed | The true cost of the China hedge | S115 |
| DMA interoperability decisions and appeals | Ongoing; 56 requests by 2026-03-22 | In progress | Whether services defaults survive regulation | S119 |

The strategy converts AI into growth through the installed base rather than through the model: a better assistant sells phones and protects high-margin services, and those services pay for the R&D the assistant requires. What must be true within twelve months is narrow and checkable. The December 2026 quarter has to show that higher prices did not break demand; Siri has to leave beta and hold quality in languages beyond English; services growth has to stay in double digits against DMA remedies; and gross margin has to absorb memory inflation without the non-recurring tariff refunds that flattered 2026. If all four hold, the company has bought time and the partnership is a bridge. If two fail, the AI expense is funding a feature that does not defend the price.

The signposts that would show the strategy failing are specific: a discount or a lower-capacity model to hold iPhone volume, a second slip in Siri availability, a fall in services growth below the rate of the installed base, or disclosure of a large multi-year model licence whose cost is not offset by hardware price. None of these is visible in the filings reviewed. The strategic risk is not that Apple loses the AI race on capability — it is that the race turns out not to be the thing that sells phones, in which case Apple wins the hardware cycle and the AI spending was a cost of staying in the conversation."}],"isError":false}

Apple is winning on profit and price and, since the September 2026 quarter, on share in a shrinking China market: it holds 65% of premium phone units at a 40.1% product gross margin, Huawei leads China 21.3% to 19.5% but Apple gained 4.8 points, and regulation caps the services take rate. The position is strengthening in hardware, contested in services by OpenAI and Alphabet at a scale no handset rival has reached, and exposed to market size rather than share loss [S5]. Apple's 10-K concedes a minority share in smartphones, PCs, tablets and wearables, so competition is mapped per product, each with a different rival set.

Huawei is the most dangerous rival to Apple's profit pool, Samsung to its unit position. Huawei led China with 21.3% to Apple's 19.5% in Q3 2026, after 22.6% to 18.1% in Q2, and IDC expects HarmonyOS shipments to nearly triple to 51M units in 2026; it funds the push with CNY192.3B of R&D, 21.8% of CNY880.9B of 2025 revenue [S96, S139, S140, S86]. Samsung is broader, with 19% global share in 2025 and 23% in Q3 2026, the only rival with scale across phones, wearables and PCs, but its MX and Networks division lost KRW0.6T in Q3 2026 despite 10.55% revenue growth, so it cannot buy share indefinitely. Xiaomi competes on price with an 8.5% handset gross margin and a 42.6% profit fall, which caps how far it can undercut before losing money. Huawei takes price and profit; Samsung takes volume and loses money doing it.

Share trends show Apple gaining value and premium ground while its global unit share moves sideways [S92, S120, S94, S84, S150]. Apple led 2025 with 20% of global units to Samsung's 19%; in Q3 2026 Samsung held 23% to Apple's 22% as the market fell 20%. The premium layer is where Apple improves: 65% of $600-plus units in H1 2026 with 9% growth, and IDC expects iOS to reach a record 23.6% share in 2026. Pricing power is partially established, not proven. Product gross margin rose to 40.1% in Q3 FY2026 from 34.5%, but the price rise is partly imposed by a memory shock, with NAND and DRAM costs more than 300% above a year earlier. Elasticity evidence is two launch windows: after the $100 iPhone 17 Pro increase in September 2025, CIRP put the US weighted average retail price at a record December-quarter $1,077 against $953 a year earlier, and iPhone 18 Pro sales rose 23.5% in the first three weeks after a further $100 rise. Both are mix-led launch observations, so full-cycle elasticity is not established.

China is where the risk has flipped from share loss to market contraction [S139, S140, S87, S6]. Q3 2026 shipments fell 10% to the lowest third-quarter level since 2012 on Counterpoint's count and 15.4% on IDC's; Apple took 19.5%, up 4.8 points, with Huawei leading at 21.3% and the two the only top brands to gain, taking 40% between them. Apple's Greater China revenue grew 30% in the first nine months of FY2026 in a market down 4.2% in H1. The vulnerability is the size and price level of the pool: IDC expects component costs elevated through much of 2027, Apple raised iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max prices by $100 and holds the standard iPhone 18 to spring 2027, so part of the Q3 gain is pull-forward and launch timing. Apple has steadied China and gained premium share without regaining structural leadership; HarmonyOS scale still gives Huawei a localisation advantage Apple cannot match.

Two competitors sit above the handset fight, and neither needs a phone to reach Apple's services wallet [S148, S149, S151, S118]. ChatGPT reached 1.2 billion weekly users by 29 September 2026, and OpenAI told investors it had about $50B of annualised revenue at end-September, 77% run-rate growth in its third quarter against Apple's 14.1% services growth in nine months, with Pro tiers at $100, $200 and $500 a month. That is 41% of Apple's $120.5B services revenue and growing faster; OpenAI is also a future hardware entrant, working with Jony Ive on a device shipping no earlier than February 2027. Microsoft attacks the layer beneath: $331.8B of FY2026 revenue, a 46.8% operating margin, $115.9B of capex and 20% of Q2 2026 cloud infrastructure spend against AWS's 28% and Google's 15% in a $143.4B quarter. Apple buys compute rather than owning it, including Google TPUs, so its AI cost curve and capability depend on rivals. Neither threatens iPhone units in 2026; both cap what Apple can charge for intelligence as a service.

Regulation transfers rent from Apple to its rivals [S77, S102, S93]. From 1 October 2026 the EU applies a 26% commission on App Store in-app purchases, 20% on alternative payment processing, 15% on link-outs and a 5% Core Technology Commission on apps distributed through alternative marketplaces or the web, after Apple was fined EUR500M for DMA non-compliance in 2025. The effect is to lower switching costs out of the App Store in a region that is 26.7% of Apple's revenue and to hand Spotify, Epic and alternative storefronts an iOS distribution channel; Spotify has 300M paying subscribers against an estimated 100-108M for Apple Music. Its spread to other jurisdictions is the regulatory risk to monitor.

| Services and AI | OpenAI in AI subscriptions; Alphabet in advertising | Apple in app distribution | Spotify in music; Microsoft in enterprise AI | DMA-enabled alternative stores | S149, S151, S93, S77 |

The status quo is formidable: consumers hold devices longer, the cheapest segment is disappearing, and IDC sees no China recovery before 2028-2029. Pipeline threats are Apple's foldable in H2 2026, HarmonyOS expansion, Gemini-integrated Pixel, OpenAI's 2027 device and AI agents that could move the assistant layer off the operating system. Apple's wedge is silicon, OS and an installed base at an all-time high in Q3 FY2026, letting it earn product margins rivals cannot match while they earn single digits or lose money; that supports profit-share gains and, in 2026, share gains inside a contracting market, but not unit growth. The competitive position therefore supports a quality-compounder view with a regulated ceiling on services, not a share-gain growth story. Confidence is medium-high on hardware and China, medium on services, because take rates, assistant usage and elasticity are still moving. Diligence questions: how much of the premium and China gain is price inflation, how much ChatGPT usage substitutes for Siri, how fast EU developers shift to external distribution, and whether Huawei can export HarmonyOS.

Two things follow. That is not a scandal; it is what a mature cash machine should do with cash it cannot reinvest at its own cost of capital. But an investor paying 39.5x is paying for the cash return, not receiving a bargain from it [S6, S1].

The multiple, not the business, is the swing factor. Apple traded at 24.6x at the end of FY2022, 27.9x in FY2023, 37.5x in FY2024 and 34.2x in FY2025; it now trades at 39.5x trailing and 35.2x forward, against a twelve-month average of 35.7x. arguments.markdown:
Apple is winning on profit and price and, since the September 2026 quarter, on share in a shrinking China market: 65% of premium phone units at a 40.1% product gross margin, Huawei ahead in China 21.3% to 19.5% but Apple up 4.8 points, and regulation capping the services take rate. It is strengthening in hardware, contested in services by OpenAI and Alphabet, and exposed to market size rather than share loss [S5].

| Competitor | Product | Technology | Regulatory status | Performance | Price | Share | Strengths vs Apple | Weaknesses vs Apple | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Samsung | Galaxy S26; Z Fold 7 | Android; Exynos or Snapdragon | Unrestricted | Flagship; foldable | Premium | 19% 2025; 23% Q3 2026 | Foldable lead; carrier reach | MX lost KRW0.6T Q3 2026 | S91, S92, S120 |
| Huawei | Mate, Pura; HarmonyOS | Kirin; HarmonyOS | China scale; US curbs | Camera, battery | Premium | 21.3% China Q3 2026 | Local supply chain; holds price | Little share outside China | S139, S140, S86 |
| Xiaomi | Xiaomi 17 | Android; Snapdragon | Unrestricted | Value flagship | Mid-premium | 11.5% global Q2 2026 | Price-performance; AIoT and EV | 8.5% handset margin; profit -42.6% | S90 |
| Alphabet (Google) | Pixel 11; Search, YouTube; Gemini | Android; Tensor; Gemini | Antitrust remedies | Ads; 15% cloud | Ad-funded; premium phones | 15% cloud Q2 2026; Pixel share not disclosed | Search, ads, cloud, Gemini | Small hardware reach; AI capex dilution | S15, S50, S151 |
| OpenAI | ChatGPT; AI subscription; Dots | GPT-6 Astra; rented cloud | AI rules pending | 1.2B weekly users; ~$50B annualised revenue | $100-500/month Pro | Not disclosed | Assistant mindshare; cross-platform | No device OS; profit not disclosed | S148, S149 |
| Microsoft | Azure, Copilot, Windows | Cloud; OpenAI models | None | $331.8B FY2026 revenue, +17.8% | Subscription | 20% cloud Q2 2026 | Enterprise channel; $115.9B capex | No phone platform | S49, S13, S151 |
| Lenovo, HP, Dell | PC lines | Windows on x86 | Unrestricted | Enterprise channel | $600-2,000 | 24.4%, 19.1%, 13.6% Q2 2026 | Price tiers | No OS-silicon integration | S95 |
| Spotify | Music; app distribution | App; DMA distribution | EU DMA beneficiary | 300M paying subscribers | Subscription | Twice Apple Music | Cross-platform; podcasts | No hardware bundle | S93, S77 |

Huawei is the most dangerous rival to Apple's profit pool, Samsung to its unit position. Huawei led China 21.3% to 19.5% in Q3 2026, after 22.6% to 18.1% in Q2, and IDC expects HarmonyOS shipments to nearly triple to 51M units in 2026, funded by CNY192.3B of R&D, 21.8% of 2025 revenue [S96, S139, S140, S86]. Samsung is broader, with scale across phones, wearables and PCs, but its MX and Networks division lost KRW0.6T in Q3 2026 despite 10.55% revenue growth, so it cannot buy share indefinitely. Huawei takes price and profit; Samsung takes volume and loses money doing it.

Apple gains value and premium ground while global unit share moves sideways [S92, S120, S94, S84, S150]. Apple led 2025 with 20% of units to Samsung's 19%; by Q3 2026 Samsung held 23% to Apple's 22%. The premium layer is where Apple improves: 65% of $600-plus units in H1 2026, and IDC expects iOS to reach a record 23.6% in 2026. Pricing power is partially established, not proven. Product gross margin rose to 40.1% in Q3 FY2026 from 34.5%, but part of the price rise is a memory shock, with NAND and DRAM costs more than 300% above a year earlier. Elasticity evidence is two launch windows: after the $100 iPhone 17 Pro increase in September 2025, CIRP put the US weighted average retail price at a record December-quarter $1,077 against $953, and iPhone 18 Pro sales rose 23.5% in the first three weeks after a further $100 rise. Both are mix-led launch observations, so full-cycle elasticity is not established.

China is where risk has flipped from share loss to market contraction [S139, S140, S87, S6]. Q3 2026 shipments fell 10% to the lowest third-quarter level since 2012 (Counterpoint) and 15.4% (IDC); Apple took 19.5%, up 4.8 points, Huawei led at 21.3%, and the two were the only top brands to gain. Apple's Greater China revenue grew 30% in nine months of FY2026. The vulnerability is the pool's size and price level: IDC expects component costs elevated through much of 2027, Apple raised iPhone 18 Pro prices by $100 and holds the standard iPhone 18 to spring 2027, so part of the gain is pull-forward. Apple has steadied China without regaining structural leadership; HarmonyOS still gives Huawei a localisation advantage.

Two competitors sit above the handset fight; neither needs a phone to reach Apple's services wallet [S148, S149, S151, S118]. ChatGPT reached 1.2 billion weekly users by 29 September 2026, and OpenAI told investors it had about $50B of annualised revenue at end-September, 77% run-rate growth in the quarter against Apple's 14.1% services growth in nine months. That is 41% of Apple's $120.5B services revenue. OpenAI is also a future hardware entrant, working with Jony Ive on a device shipping no earlier than February 2027. Microsoft attacks the layer beneath: $331.8B of FY2026 revenue at a 46.8% operating margin and 20% of Q2 2026 cloud spend to AWS's 28% and Google's 15%. Apple buys compute rather than owning it, including Google TPUs, so its AI cost curve depends on rivals.

Regulation transfers rent from Apple to rivals [S77, S102, S93]. From 1 October 2026 the EU applies a 26% commission on App Store in-app purchases and a 5% Core Technology Commission on apps distributed through alternative marketplaces or the web, after Apple was fined EUR500M for DMA non-compliance in 2025. That lowers switching costs out of the App Store in a region that is 26.7% of Apple's revenue and gives Spotify and rival storefronts an iOS channel; Spotify has 300M paying subscribers against an estimated 100-108M for Apple Music. Its spread to other jurisdictions is the risk to monitor.

| Product | Leader | Challenger | Niche player | Emerging threat | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| iPhone (premium) | Apple | Samsung | Google Pixel | Huawei in China; OpenAI's assistant layer | S94, S139, S148 |
| Mac | Lenovo by units | Apple | HP and Dell premium tiers | Snapdragon Windows PCs | S95 |
| Wearables | Xiaomi by units, Apple by value | Huawei | Oura rings, Meta glasses | OpenAI device from 2027 | S85, S148 |
| Services and AI | OpenAI in AI subscriptions; Alphabet in advertising | Apple in app distribution | Spotify in music; Microsoft in enterprise AI | DMA-enabled alternative stores | S149, S151, S93, S77 |

The status quo, doing nothing, is formidable: consumers hold devices longer, the cheapest segment is disappearing, and IDC sees no China recovery before 2028-2029. Pipeline threats are the foldable, HarmonyOS, Gemini-integrated Pixel and OpenAI's 2027 device. Apple's wedge is silicon, OS and a record installed base, letting it earn product margins rivals cannot match while they earn single digits or lose money; that supports profit-share gains and 2026 share gains inside a contracting market, but not unit growth. The position supports a quality-compounder view with a regulated ceiling on services, not a share-gain story. Confidence is medium-high on hardware and China, medium on services. Diligence questions: how much of the premium and China gain is price inflation, how much ChatGPT usage substitutes for Siri, how fast EU developers shift to external distribution, and whether Huawei can export HarmonyOS.

| Opportunities | Foldables above 17M units by 2027 at a $2,550+ ASP; services advertising; Mac share gains; Gemini-powered Siri | S84, S95, S111 |

::: evidence
**Apple's competitive advantage is profit capture, and in 2026 also China premium share, not unit leadership.**

Apple holds 20% of units but 65% of premium units and 36-43% of value (Counterpoint, S94; IDC, S84). Its 40.1% product gross margin compares with Xiaomi's 8.5% and a loss at Samsung's mobile division (S17, S90, S91). In China, Q3 2026 shipments fell 10% yet Apple's share rose 4.8 points to 19.5% behind Huawei's 21.3% (Counterpoint, S139, S96); the vulnerability is the shrinking pool and regulation (S140, S77), not lost share. The services layer is contested: ChatGPT reached 1.2 billion weekly users and OpenAI about $50B of annualised revenue (S148, S149).

arguments.markdown:
Apple's moat is real but uneven: in-house silicon, operating-system control and a 2.5-billion-device installed base are hard to replicate, while the intelligence layer this upgrade cycle is sold on is rented from Google, so AI protects the franchise without widening it. The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, announced on 2026-09-09 and on sale from 2026-09-18, start at $1,199 and $1,299, ship the 2nm A20 Pro and run iOS 27 with a Siri rebuilt on Gemini; iPhone net sales were $54.25bn in the quarter to 2026-06-27, up 22%, while R&D rose 33% to $34.04bn over nine months as capital spending fell. [S113, S6]

### The hardware cycle is being re-priced, not matured

Apple split its launch: the Pro, Pro Max and the first foldable, iPhone Duo, arrived in September 2026, while the standard iPhone 18, 18e and a second-generation Air are reported for spring 2027, and the iPhone 17 was repriced to $899. The mechanism is deliberate — sell the 2nm-constrained models into the holiday quarter and the volume models in March, when yields and memory supply have matured, turning one spike into two. The risk is elasticity: prices rose into a memory-cost cycle, and the December 2026 quarter is the first test. [S112]

### Siri shipped, two years late and in beta

Siri AI went out with iOS 27 on 2026-09-14 as an English beta, with five more languages promised for October — 23 months after Apple Intelligence shipped in October 2024, and after the personalised-Siri promise slipped in 2025. The assistant underneath is a multi-year Google Gemini deal confirmed on 2026-01-12, reported by Bloomberg at a 1.2-trillion-parameter model and $1bn a year; neither company confirmed the price. Apple's contribution is the interface, personal context, onscreen awareness, camera input and Private Cloud Compute. Ownership moved first: on 2025-12-01 Foundation Models, ML research and AI Safety and Evaluation passed under software chief Craig Federighi with Amar Subramanya as VP of AI, as John Giannandrea stepped down ahead of retirement. Apple bought what it could not ship and reorganised the rest. [S111, S122, S127]

::: evidence
**The flagship AI feature runs on a competitor's frontier model and a competitor's chips.** Google confirmed on 2026-01-12 a multi-year deal to supply Gemini for the rebuilt Siri, reported at $1bn a year and 1.2 trillion parameters, while Apple's own foundation models were trained on 8,192 Google TPU v4 and 2,048 TPU v5p chips rented through Google Cloud. Apple keeps the interface, the data boundary and the device; it does not keep the model or the compute. [S111, S118]
:::

### The licence is small per device and dangerous per query

At the reported $1bn a year the Gemini licence is 0.65% of the $154,859M trailing operating income and $0.06 of EPS — less than the $0.52 of EPS that 200 basis points of gross margin are worth on trailing revenue, and immaterial unless the pricing formula changes. Across the 2.5 billion active devices Apple disclosed on 2026-01-29, per-device pricing at $0.50, $1 and $2 a year costs $1.25bn, $2.5bn and $5.0bn, taking EPS to $0.07, $0.14 and $0.28; booked as a service it would cut services gross margin from 76.3% to 75.3%, 74.2% and 72.2%. The reported $1bn implies $0.40 a device. Apple does not disclose the classification: the visible evidence — R&D up 33% on "infrastructure-related costs, including investments in artificial intelligence" and headcount while capex fell — points to R&D, and the choice changes the margin narrative, not EPS. Per-query pricing is the tail: at an assumed 1 billion queries a day each cent a query is $3.65bn a year, and Apple discloses neither the volume nor the rate. [S6, S111, S152]

| Per-device price | Annual cost at 2.5bn devices | vs reported $1bn | Services gross margin if booked there | EPS impact | Share of TTM operating income | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $0.40, implied by $1bn | $1.00bn | — | 75.5% | $0.06 | 0.65% | S111, S152, S6 |
| $0.50 | $1.25bn | +25% | 75.3% | $0.07 | 0.81% | S6, S152 |
| $1.00 | $2.50bn | 2.5x | 74.2% | $0.14 | 1.61% | S6, S152 |
| $2.00 | $5.00bn | 5.0x | 72.2% | $0.28 | 3.23% | S6, S152 |

| Metric | Value | Method | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| A20 Pro process node | 2nm (A19: 3nm) | Apple launch specification | S113, S112 |
| Siri AI availability | English beta from 2026-09-14 | Apple release | S113 |
| Assistant model scale | 1.2tn parameters, reported | Press reports, unconfirmed | S122 |
| Active installed base | More than 2.5bn devices | Company release, 2026-01-29 | S152 |
| R&D, nine months to 2026-06-27 | $34.04bn, +33% | 10-Q | S6 |
| Capex, nine months to 2026-06-27 | $6.80bn (prior year $9.47bn) | 10-Q cash-flow statement | S6 |

### Silicon is the layer still widening

The A20 Pro's move to 2nm from the A19's 3nm, and the in-house C2 modem reported across the iPhone 18 line, are the parts of the stack Apple owns end to end. At a fixed retail price a node advantage becomes either margin or performance, and insourcing the modem removes a royalty and gives Apple control of cellular power and cost. The offset is memory: the June 2026 filing expects advanced-semiconductor, NAND and DRAM constraints to intensify, and products gross margin already leans on tariff refunds that will not recur. [S112, S6]

| Dimension | Apple | Google | Samsung | Huawei | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Silicon | In-house A-series, 2nm | In-house Tensor | External suppliers | In-house Kirin | S113, S112 |
| Frontier model | Licensed Gemini | Owns Gemini | Licenses Google | In-house stack | S111 |
| AI compute | Rented Google TPUs | Own TPUs and datacentres | Rents cloud | Domestic cloud | S118 |
| AI organisation | Under Software Engineering since 2025-12-01 | DeepMind | Own research | Own research | S127 |
| Distribution | Own devices and services | Android, Pixel, search | Devices | China-led | S111 |

### Where the moat actually sits

| Barrier | Difficulty (1-10) | Why | Time to replicate | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Silicon design and process access | 8 | Custom SoC, 2nm allocation, modem integration | 4-6 years | S113, S112 |
| OS and installed-base switching costs | 9 | Continuity, App Store, 76.3% services margin | 7+ years | S6, S152 |
| Manufacturing process know-how | 6 | AI-matched hinge, confocal scanning, 25 printed micro-layers | 3-4 years | S114 |
| Frontier AI model | 3 | Bought from Google, no frontier training at scale | 1-2 years, by licence | S111, S118 |
| Developer and services ecosystem | 8 | $91.73bn nine-month services revenue, defaults under pressure | 5+ years | S6 |
| **Composite moat** | **Strong hardware, weak AI** | Hardware barrier real, intelligence barrier rented | Years on hardware | S113, S6 |

The replication test favours hardware. A funded team of fifty with every published patent could match a Duo-class hinge in a few years and an A-series-class chip only after a full node cycle, and would still lack the installed base; the assistant can be licensed rather than built, as Apple did.

### Wearables, health and Vision are optionality, not a second engine

Health is the most credible adjacency: hypertension notifications on Apple Watch carry FDA clearance and peer-reviewed scrutiny in *Hypertension*, which questions whether the alerts are accurate and useful, and it is a monthly alert rather than a measurement, so the clinical claim is narrow. Vision Pro remains inside Wearables with no disclosed revenue and no confirmed successor. Both deepen the installed base and add upgrade reasons; they are sold as features, not platforms with their own economics. [S124, S5]

| Product | Stage | Launch | Revenue or share | Margin | Next milestone | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| iPhone 18 Pro / Pro Max | Shipping | 2026-09-18 | iPhone $54.25bn in Q3 FY2026, +22% | Not disclosed by model | December 2026 mix | S113, S6 |
| iPhone Duo (foldable) | Shipping | Announced 2026-09-09 | Not disclosed | Not disclosed | Durability and returns | S114 |
| Services | Shipping | Ongoing | $91.73bn in nine months, +14% | 76.3% | DMA compliance | S6 |
| Wearables and Vision Pro | Shipping | Watch Series 11, Ultra 3, SE 3 in FY2025 | Not separately disclosed | Not disclosed | Health-feature adoption | S5, S124 |

### The patent position is broad, thinning and hard to verify

U.S. grants fell to 2,722 in 2025 from 3,082 in 2024, a 12% decline and seventh place in the U.S. ranking; the portfolio is broad rather than anchored in one blocking family. No individual patent number is cited because none could be verified against a USPTO record; freedom-to-operate risk sits in foldable hinges, displays and health sensing, where verification matters most.

| Patent or portfolio | Area | Jurisdiction | Filed | Granted | Status | Relevance | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| U.S. utility grants, 2025 | Silicon, RF, display, health | US | — | 2,722 grants (2024: 3,082; rank 7th) | Granted, down 12% | Breadth, no blocking family | S117 |
| Foldable hinge and display assemblies | Hinge, crease, lamination | US, CN, EU (reported) | Not disclosed | Not disclosed | Pending and granted, unverified | Duo durability | S114 |
| On-device inference efficiency | Routing, model compression | Not verified | — | — | Published research, no patent number | Inference cost | S52, S53 |

If Siri AI leaves beta with usage data showing Apple's integration beating standalone assistants, the AI layer is worth more than a licensed feature; silence after the 2026-11-02 results would confirm the current reading. If the Gemini term is a bridge to its own model, the dependency is temporary. Until then the technology case rests on silicon, yield and switching costs, and the AI case rests on distribution. Confidence is high on machine facts, medium on model economics, low on patents.

arguments.markdown:
Apple is winning on profit and price and, since the September 2026 quarter, on share in a shrinking China market: 65% of premium phone units at a 40.1% product gross margin, Huawei ahead in China 21.3% to 19.5% but Apple up 4.8 points, and regulation capping the services take rate. It is strengthening in hardware, contested in services by OpenAI and Alphabet, and exposed to market size rather than share loss [S5].

| Alphabet (Google) | Pixel 11; Search, YouTube; Gemini | Android; Tensor; Gemini | Antitrust remedies | Ads; 15% cloud | Ad-funded; premium phones | 15% cloud Q2 2026; Pixel share not disclosed | Search, ads, cloud, Gemini | Small hardware reach; AI capex dilution | S15, S50, S151 |
| OpenAI | ChatGPT; AI subscription; Dots | GPT-6 Astra; rented cloud | AI rules pending | 1.2B weekly users; ~$50B annualised revenue | $100-500/month Pro | Not disclosed | Assistant mindshare; cross-platform | No device OS; profit not disclosed | S148, S149 |
| Microsoft | Azure, Copilot, Windows | Cloud; OpenAI models | None | $331.8B FY2026 revenue, +17.8% | Subscription | 20% cloud Q2 2026 | Enterprise channel; $115.9B capex | No phone platform | S49, S13, S151 |
| Lenovo, HP, Dell | PC lines | Windows on x86 | Unrestricted | Enterprise channel | $600-2,000 | 24.4%, 19.1%, 13.6% Q2 2026 | Price tiers | No OS-silicon integration | S95 |
| Spotify | Music; app distribution | App; DMA distribution | EU DMA beneficiary | 300M paying subscribers | Subscription | Twice Apple Music | Cross-platform; podcasts | No hardware bundle | S93, S77 |

Huawei is the most dangerous rival to Apple's profit pool, Samsung to its unit position. Huawei led China 21.3% to 19.5% in Q3 2026, after 22.6% to 18.1% in Q2, and IDC expects HarmonyOS shipments to nearly triple to 51M units in 2026, funded by CNY192.3B of R&D, 21.8% of 2025 revenue [S96, S139, S140, S86]. Samsung is broader, with scale across phones, wearables and PCs, but its MX and Networks division lost KRW0.6T in Q3 2026 despite 10.55% revenue growth. Huawei takes price and Samsung volume, at a loss.

Apple's global unit share was 20% in 2025 to Samsung's 19%, and 22% to Samsung's 23% in Q3 2026, so its position moves sideways even as value capture rises [S92, S120, S94, S84, S150]. The premium layer is where Apple improves: 65% of $600-plus units in H1 2026, and IDC expects iOS to reach a record 23.6% in 2026. Pricing power is partially established, not proven. Product gross margin rose to 40.1% in Q3 FY2026 from 34.5%, but part of the price rise is a memory shock, with NAND and DRAM costs more than 300% above a year earlier. The mechanism is mix: a $100 Pro increase lifts revenue per unit even if unit demand is flat. Elasticity evidence is two launch windows: after the $100 iPhone 17 Pro increase in September 2025, CIRP put the US weighted average retail price at a record December-quarter $1,077 against $953, and iPhone 18 Pro sales rose 23.5% in the first three weeks after a further $100 rise. Both are mix-led launch windows; full-cycle elasticity is not established.

China is where risk has flipped from share loss to market contraction [S139, S140, S87, S6]. Q3 2026 shipments fell 10% to the lowest third-quarter level since 2012 (Counterpoint) and 15.4% (IDC); Apple took 19.5%, up 4.8 points, Huawei led at 21.3%, and the two were the only top brands to gain. Apple's Greater China revenue grew 30% in nine months of FY2026. The vulnerability is the pool's size and price level: IDC expects component costs elevated through much of 2027, Apple raised iPhone 18 Pro prices by $100 and holds the standard iPhone 18 to spring 2027, so part of the gain is pull-forward. Apple has steadied China without regaining structural leadership; HarmonyOS still gives Huawei a localisation advantage.

Two competitors sit above the handset fight; neither needs a phone to reach Apple's services wallet [S148, S149, S151, S118]. ChatGPT reached 1.2 billion weekly users by 29 September 2026, and OpenAI told investors it had about $50B of annualised revenue at end-September, 77% run-rate growth in the quarter against Apple's 14.1% services growth in nine months. That is 41% of Apple's $120.5B services revenue. OpenAI is also a future hardware entrant, working with Jony Ive on a device shipping no earlier than February 2027. Microsoft attacks the layer beneath: $331.8B of FY2026 revenue at a 46.8% operating margin and 20% of Q2 2026 cloud spend to AWS's 28% and Google's 15%. Apple buys compute rather than owning it, including Google TPUs, so its AI cost curve depends on rivals.

Regulation transfers rent from Apple to rivals [S77, S102, S93]. From 1 October 2026 the EU applies a 26% commission on App Store in-app purchases and a 5% Core Technology Commission on apps distributed through alternative marketplaces or the web, after Apple was fined EUR500M for DMA non-compliance in 2025. That lowers switching costs in a region that is 26.7% of Apple's revenue and gives Spotify and rival storefronts an iOS channel; Spotify has 300M paying subscribers against an estimated 100-108M for Apple Music. Its spread to other jurisdictions is the risk to monitor.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| iPhone (premium) | Leader | Apple | Samsung | Google Pixel | Huawei in China; OpenAI's assistant layer | S94, S139, S148 |
| Mac | Share gainer | Lenovo by units | Apple | HP and Dell premium tiers | Snapdragon Windows PCs | S95 |
| Wearables | Leader by value | Xiaomi by units | Huawei | Oura rings, Meta glasses | OpenAI device from 2027 | S85, S148 |
| Services and AI | Challenger | OpenAI in AI subscriptions; Alphabet in advertising | Apple in app distribution | Spotify in music; Microsoft in enterprise AI | DMA-enabled alternative stores | S149, S151, S93, S77 |

The status quo, doing nothing, is formidable: consumers hold devices longer, the cheapest segment is disappearing, and IDC sees no China recovery before 2028-2029. Pipeline threats: the foldable, HarmonyOS, Gemini-powered Pixel and OpenAI's 2027 device. Apple's wedge is silicon, OS and a record installed base, letting it earn product margins rivals cannot match while they earn single digits or lose money; that supports profit-share gains and 2026 share gains inside a contracting market, but not unit growth. That supports a quality-compounder view with a regulated services ceiling, not a share-gain story. Confidence is medium-high on hardware and China, medium on services. Diligence questions: how much of the premium and China gain is price inflation, how much ChatGPT usage substitutes for Siri, how fast EU developers shift to external distribution, and whether Huawei can export HarmonyOS.

|---|---|---|

| Weaknesses | 19.5% China share behind Huawei's 21.3% in a market down 10%; 15.5% wearables share; no advertising or cloud scale; one-product concentration | S139, S85, S5, S151 |
| Opportunities | Foldables above 17M units by 2027 at a $2,550+ ASP; services advertising; Mac share gains; Gemini-powered Siri | S84, S95, S111 |
| Threats | DMA 5% fee on external distribution; Huawei premium share; memory costs up more than 300%; OpenAI's 1.2B users and 2027 device; full-cycle elasticity not established | S77, S87, S148, S150 |
:::

::: evidence
**Apple's competitive advantage is profit capture, and in 2026 also China premium share, not unit leadership.**

Apple holds 20% of units but 65% of premium units and 36-43% of value (Counterpoint, S94; IDC, S84). In China, Q3 2026 shipments fell 10% yet Apple's share rose 4.8 points to 19.5% behind Huawei's 21.3% (Counterpoint, S139, S96); the vulnerability is the shrinking pool and regulation (S140, S77), not lost share. The services layer is contested: ChatGPT reached 1.2 billion weekly users and OpenAI about $50B of annualised revenue (S148, S149).
:::

arguments.markdown:
Apple's moat is real but uneven: in-house silicon, operating-system control and a 2.5-billion-device installed base are hard to replicate, while the intelligence layer this upgrade cycle sells on is rented from Google, so AI protects the franchise without widening it. iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, announced on 2026-09-09 and on sale from 2026-09-18, start at $1,199 and $1,299, ship the 2nm A20 Pro and run iOS 27 with Siri rebuilt on Gemini; iPhone net sales were $54.25bn in the quarter to 2026-06-27, up 22%, while R&D rose 33% to $34.04bn over nine months as capex fell. [S113, S6]

### The hardware cycle is being re-priced, not matured

Apple split its launch: the Pro, Pro Max and the first foldable, iPhone Duo, arrived in September 2026; the standard iPhone 18, 18e and Air 2 are reported for spring 2027, and the iPhone 17 was repriced to $899. Selling the 2nm-constrained models into the holiday quarter and the volume models in March turns one spike into two. Prices rose into a memory-cost cycle, and the December 2026 quarter is the first test. [S112]

### Siri shipped, two years late and in beta

Siri AI went out with iOS 27 on 2026-09-14 as an English beta, five more languages promised for October — 23 months after Apple Intelligence shipped in October 2024, and after the personalised-Siri promise slipped in 2025. The assistant underneath is a multi-year Google Gemini deal confirmed on 2026-01-12, reported by Bloomberg at a 1.2-trillion-parameter model and $1bn a year; neither company confirmed the price. Apple contributes the interface, personal context, camera input and Private Cloud Compute. Ownership moved first: on 2025-12-01 Foundation Models, ML research and AI safety passed to software chief Craig Federighi, with Amar Subramanya as VP of AI, as John Giannandrea stepped down ahead of retirement. Apple bought what it could not ship. [S111, S122, S127]

::: evidence
**The flagship AI feature runs on a competitor's frontier model and a competitor's chips.** Google confirmed on 2026-01-12 a multi-year deal to supply Gemini for the rebuilt Siri, reported at $1bn a year, while Apple's own foundation models were trained on 8,192 Google TPU v4 and 2,048 TPU v5p chips rented through Google Cloud. Apple keeps the interface and the device; not the model or the compute. [S111, S118]
:::

### The licence is small per device and dangerous per query

At the reported $1bn a year the Gemini licence is 0.65% of the $154,859M trailing operating income and $0.06 of EPS, below the $0.52 that 200 basis points of gross margin are worth. Across the 2.5 billion active devices Apple disclosed on 2026-01-29, $0.50, $1 and $2 per device a year cost $1.25bn, $2.5bn and $5.0bn, taking EPS to $0.07, $0.14 and $0.28; booked as a service they would cut services gross margin from 76.3% to 75.3%, 74.2% and 72.2%. The $1bn implies $0.40 a device. Apple does not disclose the classification; R&D up 33% on "infrastructure-related costs, including investments in artificial intelligence" while capex fell points to R&D, and the choice changes the margin narrative, not EPS. The tail is per-query pricing: at an assumed 1 billion queries a day each cent is $3.65bn a year, and Apple discloses neither volume nor rate. [S6, S111, S152]

| $0.40, implied by $1bn | $1.00bn | — | 75.5% | $0.06 | 0.65% | S111, S152, S6 |

### Silicon is the layer still widening

The A20 Pro's move to 2nm from the A19's 3nm, and the in-house C2 modem reported across the iPhone 18 line, are the parts of the stack Apple owns end to end. At a fixed price a node advantage becomes margin or performance, and insourcing the modem removes a royalty and gives Apple control of cellular power and cost. The offset is memory: the June 2026 filing expects semiconductor, NAND and DRAM constraints to intensify, and products gross margin already leans on tariff refunds that will not recur. [S112, S6]

### Where the moat actually sits

| Barrier | Difficulty (1-10) | Why | Time to replicate | Source |

| Manufacturing process know-how | 6 | AI-matched hinge, confocal scanning, printed micro-layers | 3-4 years | S114 |
| Frontier AI model | 3 | Bought from Google, no frontier training at scale | 1-2 years, by licence | S111, S118 |
| Developer and services ecosystem | 8 | $91.73bn nine-month services revenue, defaults under pressure | 5+ years | S6 |
| **Composite moat** | **Strong hardware, weak AI** | Hardware barrier real, intelligence barrier rented | Years on hardware | S113, S6 |

The replication test favours hardware: a funded team of fifty with every published patent could match a Duo-class hinge in a few years and an A-series-class chip only after a full node cycle, and would still lack the installed base; the assistant can be licensed, as Apple did.

### Wearables, health and Vision are optionality, not a second engine

Health is the most credible adjacency: hypertension notifications on Apple Watch carry FDA clearance and peer-reviewed scrutiny in *Hypertension*, which questions their accuracy and usefulness; a monthly alert is not a measurement, so the clinical claim is narrow. Vision Pro sits inside Wearables with no disclosed revenue and no confirmed successor. Both deepen the installed base and add upgrade reasons, but are sold as features, not platforms with their own economics. [S124, S5]

| iPhone Duo (foldable) | Shipping | Announced 2026-09-09 | Not disclosed | Not disclosed | Durability and returns | S114 |
| Services | Shipping | Ongoing | $91.73bn in nine months, +14% | 76.3% | DMA compliance | S6 |
| Wearables and Vision Pro | Shipping | Watch Series 11, Ultra 3, SE 3 in FY2025 | Not separately disclosed | Not disclosed | Health-feature adoption | S5, S124 |

### The patent position is broad, thinning and hard to verify

U.S. grants fell to 2,722 in 2025 from 3,082 in 2024, a 12% decline and seventh place in the U.S. ranking; the portfolio is broad rather than anchored in one blocking family. No individual patent number is cited because none could be verified against a USPTO record; freedom-to-operate risk sits in foldable hinges, displays and health sensing, where verification matters most.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| U.S. utility grants, 2025 | Silicon, RF, display, health | US | — | 2,722 grants (2024: 3,082; rank 7th) | Granted, down 12% | Breadth, no blocking family | S117 |
| Foldable hinge and display assemblies | Hinge, crease, lamination | US, CN, EU (reported) | Not disclosed | Not disclosed | Pending and granted, unverified | Duo durability | S114 |
| On-device inference efficiency | Routing, model compression | Not verified | — | — | Published research, no patent number | Inference cost | S52, S53 |

If Siri AI leaves beta with usage data showing its integration beats standalone assistants, the layer is worth more than a licensed feature; silence after the 2026-11-02 results confirms the current reading. If the Gemini term is a bridge to its own model, the dependency is temporary. Until then the technology case rests on silicon, yield and switching costs, and the AI case rests on distribution. Confidence is high on machine facts, medium on model economics, low on patents.

arguments.markdown:
Apple is winning on profit and price and, since the September 2026 quarter, on share in a shrinking China market: a 65% share of premium phone units at a 40.1% product gross margin, Huawei ahead in China 21.3% to 19.5% but Apple up 4.8 points, and regulation capping the services take rate. It is strengthening in hardware, contested in services by OpenAI and Alphabet, and exposed to market size rather than share loss [S5].

| OpenAI | ChatGPT; AI subscription; Dots | GPT-6 Astra; rented cloud | AI rules pending | 1.2B weekly users; ~$50B annualised revenue | $100-500/month Pro | Not disclosed | Assistant mindshare; cross-platform | No device OS; profit not disclosed | S148, S149 |
| Microsoft | Azure, Copilot, Windows | Cloud; OpenAI models | None | $331.8B FY2026 revenue, +17.8% | Subscription | 20% cloud Q2 2026 | Enterprise channel; $115.9B capex | No phone platform | S49, S13, S151 |
| Lenovo, HP, Dell | PC lines | Windows on x86 | Unrestricted | Enterprise channel | $600-2,000 | 24.4%, 19.1%, 13.6% Q2 2026 | Price tiers | No OS-silicon integration | S95 |
| Spotify | Music; app distribution | App; DMA distribution | EU DMA beneficiary | 300M paying subscribers | Subscription | Twice Apple Music | Cross-platform; podcasts | No hardware bundle | S93, S77 |

Huawei is the most dangerous rival to Apple's profit pool, Samsung to its unit position. Huawei led China 21.3% to 19.5% in Q3 2026, after 22.6% to 18.1% in Q2, and IDC expects HarmonyOS shipments to nearly triple to 51M units in 2026, funded by CNY192.3B of R&D, 21.8% of 2025 revenue [S96, S139, S140, S86]. Samsung is broader, with scale across phones, wearables and PCs, but its MX and Networks division lost KRW0.6T in Q3 2026 despite 10.55% revenue growth. Huawei takes price and Samsung volume, at a loss.

Apple's global smartphone market share was 20% in 2025 to Samsung's 19%, and 22% in Q3 2026 to Samsung's 23%, so its position moves sideways even as value capture rises [S92, S120, S94, S84, S150]. The premium layer is where Apple improves: a 65% share of $600-plus units in H1 2026, and IDC expects iOS to reach a record 23.6% in 2026. Pricing power is partially established, not proven, because part of the price rise is a memory shock, with NAND and DRAM costs more than 300% above a year earlier. The mechanism is mix: a $100 Pro increase lifts revenue per unit even if unit demand is flat. Elasticity evidence is two launch windows: after the $100 iPhone 17 Pro increase in September 2025, CIRP put the US weighted average retail price at a record December-quarter $1,077 against $953, and iPhone 18 Pro sales rose 23.5% in the first three weeks after a further $100 rise. Both are mix-led launch windows, therefore full-cycle elasticity is not established.

China is where risk has flipped from share loss to market contraction [S139, S140, S87, S6]. Q3 2026 shipments fell 10% to the lowest third-quarter level since 2012 (Counterpoint) and 15.4% (IDC); Apple took 19.5%, up 4.8 points, Huawei led at 21.3%, and the two were the only top brands to gain. Apple's Greater China revenue grew 30% in nine months of FY2026. The vulnerability is the pool's size and price level: IDC expects component costs elevated through much of 2027, Apple raised iPhone 18 Pro prices by $100 and holds the standard iPhone 18 to spring 2027, so part of the gain is pull-forward. Apple has steadied China without regaining structural leadership; HarmonyOS still gives Huawei a localisation advantage.

Two competitors sit above the handset fight; neither needs a phone to reach Apple's services wallet [S148, S149, S151, S118]. ChatGPT reached 1.2 billion weekly users by 29 September 2026, and OpenAI told investors it had about $50B of annualised revenue at end-September, 77% run-rate growth in the quarter against Apple's 14.1% services growth in nine months. That is 41% of Apple's $120.5B services revenue. OpenAI is also a future hardware entrant, working with Jony Ive on a device shipping no earlier than February 2027. Microsoft attacks the layer beneath: $331.8B of FY2026 revenue at a 46.8% operating margin and 20% of Q2 2026 cloud spend to AWS's 28% and Google's 15%. Apple buys compute rather than owning it, including Google TPUs, so its AI cost curve depends on rivals.

Regulation transfers rent from Apple to rivals [S77, S102, S93]. From 1 October 2026 the EU applies a 26% commission on App Store in-app purchases and a 5% Core Technology Commission on apps distributed through alternative marketplaces or the web, after Apple was fined EUR500M for DMA non-compliance in 2025. That lowers switching costs in a region that is 26.7% of Apple's revenue and gives Spotify and rival storefronts an iOS channel; Spotify has 300M paying subscribers against an estimated 100-108M for Apple Music. Its spread to other jurisdictions is the risk to monitor.

| Wearables | Leader by value | Xiaomi by units | Huawei | Oura rings, Meta glasses | OpenAI device from 2027 | S85, S148 |
| Services and AI | Challenger | OpenAI in AI subscriptions; Alphabet in advertising | Apple in app distribution | Spotify in music; Microsoft in enterprise AI | DMA-enabled alternative stores | S149, S151, S93, S77 |

The status quo, doing nothing, is formidable: consumers hold devices longer, the cheapest segment is disappearing, and IDC sees no China recovery before 2028-2029. Pipeline threats: the foldable, HarmonyOS, Gemini-powered Pixel and OpenAI's 2027 device. Apple's wedge is silicon, OS and a record installed base, which means it earns product margins rivals cannot match while they earn single digits or lose money; that supports profit-share gains and 2026 share gains inside a contracting market, but not unit growth. That supports a quality-compounder view with a regulated services ceiling, not a share-gain story. Confidence is medium-high on hardware and China, medium on services. Diligence questions: how much of the premium and China gain is price inflation, how much ChatGPT usage substitutes for Siri, how fast EU developers shift to external distribution, and whether Huawei can export HarmonyOS.

arguments.markdown:
Apple's moat is real but uneven: in-house silicon, operating-system control and a 2.5-billion-device installed base are hard to replicate, while the intelligence layer this cycle sells on is rented from Google, so AI protects the franchise without widening it. iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, announced on 2026-09-09 and on sale from 2026-09-18, start at $1,199 and $1,299, ship the 2nm A20 Pro and run iOS 27 with Siri rebuilt on Gemini; iPhone net sales were $54.25bn in the quarter to 2026-06-27, up 22%, while R&D rose 33% to $34.04bn over nine months as capex fell. [S113, S6]

### The hardware cycle is being re-priced, not matured

Apple split its launch: the Pro, Pro Max and the first foldable, iPhone Duo, arrived in September 2026; the standard iPhone 18, 18e and Air 2 are reported for spring 2027, and the iPhone 17 was cut to $899. Selling the 2nm-constrained models into the holiday quarter and the volume models in March turns one spike into two. Prices rose into a memory-cost cycle, and the December 2026 quarter is the first test. [S112]

### Siri shipped, two years late and in beta

Siri AI went out with iOS 27 on 2026-09-14 as an English beta, five more languages promised for October — 23 months after Apple Intelligence shipped in October 2024, and after the personalised-Siri promise slipped in 2025. The assistant underneath is a multi-year Google Gemini deal confirmed on 2026-01-12, reported by Bloomberg at a 1.2-trillion-parameter model and $1bn a year; neither confirmed the price. Apple contributes the interface, personal context, camera input and Private Cloud Compute. Ownership moved first: on 2025-12-01 Foundation Models, ML research and AI safety passed to software chief Craig Federighi, with Amar Subramanya as VP of AI, as John Giannandrea stepped down ahead of retirement. Apple bought what it could not ship. [S111, S122, S127]

::: evidence
**The flagship AI feature runs on a competitor's frontier model and a competitor's chips.** Google confirmed on 2026-01-12 a multi-year deal to supply Gemini for the rebuilt Siri, reported at $1bn a year, while Apple's own foundation models were trained on 8,192 Google TPU v4 and 2,048 TPU v5p chips rented through Google Cloud. Apple keeps the interface; not the model or the compute. [S111, S118]
:::

### The licence is small per device and dangerous per query

At the reported $1bn a year the Gemini licence is 0.65% of the $154,859M trailing operating income and $0.06 of EPS, below the $0.52 that 200 basis points of gross margin are worth. Across the 2.5 billion active devices Apple disclosed on 2026-01-29, $0.50, $1 and $2 per device a year cost $1.25bn, $2.5bn and $5.0bn, taking EPS to $0.07, $0.14 and $0.28; booked as a service they would cut services gross margin from 76.3% to 75.3%, 74.2% and 72.2%. The $1bn implies $0.40 a device. Apple does not disclose the classification; R&D up 33% on "infrastructure-related costs, including investments in artificial intelligence" while capex fell points to R&D, and the choice changes the margin narrative, not EPS. The tail is per-query pricing: at an assumed 1 billion queries a day each cent is $3.65bn a year; Apple discloses neither volume nor rate. [S6, S111, S152]

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $0.40, implied by $1bn | $1.00bn | — | 75.5% | $0.06 | 0.65% | S111, S152, S6 |
| $0.50 | $1.25bn | +25% | 75.3% | $0.07 | 0.81% | S6, S152 |
| $1.00 | $2.50bn | 2.5x | 74.2% | $0.14 | 1.61% | S6, S152 |
| $2.00 | $5.00bn | 5.0x | 72.2% | $0.28 | 3.23% | S6, S152 |

| Metric | Value | Method | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| A20 Pro process node | 2nm (A19: 3nm) | Apple launch specification | S113, S112 |
| Siri AI availability | English beta from 2026-09-14 | Apple release | S113 |
| Active installed base | More than 2.5bn devices | Company release, 2026-01-29 | S152 |
| R&D, nine months to 2026-06-27 | $34.04bn, +33% | 10-Q | S6 |
| Capex, nine months to 2026-06-27 | $6.80bn (prior year $9.47bn) | 10-Q cash-flow statement | S6 |

### Silicon is the layer still widening

The A20 Pro's move to 2nm from the A19's 3nm, and the in-house C2 modem across the iPhone 18 line, are the parts Apple owns end to end. At a fixed price a node advantage becomes margin or performance, and insourcing the modem removes a royalty and gives Apple control of cellular power and cost. The offset is memory: the June 2026 filing expects semiconductor, NAND and DRAM constraints to intensify, and products gross margin already leans on tariff refunds that will not recur. [S112, S6]

| Dimension | Apple | Google | Samsung | Huawei | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Silicon | In-house A-series, 2nm | In-house Tensor | External suppliers | In-house Kirin | S113, S112 |
| Frontier model | Licensed Gemini | Owns Gemini | Licenses Google | In-house stack | S111 |
| AI compute | Rented Google TPUs | Own TPUs and datacentres | Rents cloud | Domestic cloud | S118 |
| AI organisation | Under Software Engineering since 2025-12-01 | DeepMind | Own research | Own research | S127 |

### Where the moat actually sits

| Barrier | Difficulty (1-10) | Why | Time to replicate | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Silicon design and process access | 8 | Custom SoC, 2nm allocation, modem integration | 4-6 years | S113, S112 |
| OS and installed-base switching costs | 9 | Continuity, App Store, 76.3% services margin | 7+ years | S6, S152 |
| Manufacturing process know-how | 6 | AI-matched hinge, confocal scanning, printed layers | 3-4 years | S114 |
| Frontier AI model | 3 | Bought from Google, no frontier training at scale | 1-2 years, by licence | S111, S118 |
| Developer and services ecosystem | 8 | $91.73bn nine-month services revenue, defaults under pressure | 5+ years | S6 |
| **Composite moat** | **Strong hardware, weak AI** | Hardware barrier real, intelligence barrier rented | Years on hardware | S113, S6 |

The replication test favours hardware: a funded team of fifty with every published patent could match a Duo-class hinge in a few years and an A-series-class chip only after a full node cycle, and would still lack the installed base; the assistant can be licensed, as Apple did.

### Wearables, health and Vision are optionality, not a second engine

Health is the most credible adjacency: hypertension notifications on Apple Watch carry FDA clearance and peer-reviewed scrutiny in *Hypertension*, which questions their accuracy; a monthly alert is not a measurement, so the claim is narrow. Vision Pro sits inside Wearables with no disclosed revenue and no confirmed successor. Both add upgrade reasons and are sold as features, not platforms with their own economics. [S124, S5]

| Product | Stage | Launch | Revenue or share | Margin | Next milestone | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| iPhone 18 Pro / Pro Max | Shipping | 2026-09-18 | iPhone $54.25bn in Q3 FY2026, +22% | Not disclosed by model | December 2026 mix | S113, S6 |
| iPhone Duo (foldable) | Shipping | Announced 2026-09-09 | Not disclosed | Not disclosed | Durability and returns | S114 |
| Services | Shipping | Ongoing | $91.73bn in nine months, +14% | 76.3% | DMA compliance | S6 |
| Wearables and Vision Pro | Shipping | Watch Series 11, Ultra 3, SE 3 (FY2025) | Not separately disclosed | Not disclosed | Health-feature adoption | S5, S124 |

### The patent position is broad, thinning and hard to verify

U.S. grants fell to 2,722 in 2025 from 3,082 in 2024, a 12% decline and seventh place; the portfolio is broad rather than anchored in one blocking family. No individual patent number is cited because none could be verified against a USPTO record; freedom-to-operate risk sits in foldable hinges, displays and health sensing, where verification matters most.

| Patent or portfolio | Area | Jurisdiction | Filed | Granted | Status | Relevance | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| U.S. utility grants, 2025 | Silicon, RF, display, health | US | — | 2,722 grants (2024: 3,082; rank 7th) | Granted, down 12% | Breadth, no blocking family | S117 |
| Foldable hinge and display assemblies | Hinge, crease, lamination | US, CN, EU (reported) | Not disclosed | Not disclosed | Pending and granted, unverified | Duo durability | S114 |
| On-device inference efficiency | Routing, model compression | Not verified | — | — | Published research, no patent number | Inference cost | S52, S53 |

If Siri AI leaves beta with usage data showing its integration beats standalone assistants, the layer is worth more than a licensed feature; silence after 2026-11-02 confirms this reading. If the Gemini term is a bridge to its own model, the dependency is temporary. Until then the technology case rests on silicon, yield and switching costs, and the AI case rests on distribution. Confidence is high on machine facts, medium on model economics, low on patents.

Apple's markets are large but no longer volume-growth markets: the smartphone unit pool is contracting at the fastest rate on record in 2026 while its dollar value rises, so revenue growth to 2030 must come from holding more than 40% of smartphone value, monetising a record installed base through services, and a foldable and AI-driven upgrade cycle, not from market growth. Apple's revenue compounded at 3.3% from FY2021 to FY2025 ($365.8B to $416.2B) and then accelerated to 16% in the first nine months of FY2026, with iPhone revenue up 22% [S5, S6].

SAM: the premium segment (29% of units at $600 or more) plus the iOS installed base for services, where Apple's 65% premium share sets the addressable pool. IDC attributes part of the China strength to buyers pulling purchases forward ahead of Apple's own second-half price increases and warns China's decline could widen to 20% in H2 2026. The sub-$100 segment, 173M units in 2025, fell nearly 60% in Q2 2026. Apple's profit is unusually cash-true. Over the twelve months to 27 June 2026 operating cash flow was $146,724M, capital expenditure $10,041M and free cash flow $136,683M against net income of $128,930M — a headline conversion of 1.06x, or 0.97x on a normalised $125,084M, on capex of 2.2% of revenue, against 0.50x and 34.9% at Microsoft and 0.08x and 33.9% at Alphabet. Revenue grew from $383,285M in FY2023 to $416,161M in FY2025 and $466,823M trailing, with operating margin of 29.8%, 32.0% and 33.2%. ### The margin is the record, and part of it was purchased

Gross margin went from 44.1% in FY2023 to 46.2%, 46.9%, 49.1% in the nine months of FY2026 and 48.7% trailing, and the June 2026 quarter printed 50.1%, a record. Nine months reconcile exactly: products gross profit of $108,819M on $272,629M is 39.9%, services $69,963M on $91,728M is 76.3%, summing to the filed $178,782M; the quarter ran at 40.1% and 75.6%, so applying 40.1% to nine-month products would overstate gross profit by about $0.5B. Services earn 40.3% of the trailing $227,123M gross-profit pool on 25.8% of revenue at 76.0%. The 30 July 2026 release attributes 2 points of the quarter's gross margin and $0.11 of $2.02 EPS to tariff refunds. The cost side has turned: memory prices rose 146% in the first quarter of 2026 against the 2025 average and the 10-Q expects the component trends "to intensify". A 47-48% gross margin, not 50.1%, is the level to capitalise. [S6, S17, S68]

:::

### Cash conversion is real, but a liability accrual did the lifting

Nine-month operating cash flow rose $35,242M to $116,996M while net income rose $16,920M; working capital supplied $16,366M of the gap. The dominant line is other current and non-current liabilities, +$10,016M against −$15,161M a year earlier. Other non-current liabilities rose $13,531M to $55,080M while other current liabilities fell $4,128M to $62,259M, a combined $9,403M build reconciling within $613M; the prior year carries the ~$15.8B Irish State Aid settlement (cash taxes of $37,332M against a $15,381M provision). The line's clean history is $3,031M in FY2023, −$248M in FY2024 and $4,724M in FY2025, a $2,502M average, so the $14,101M it puts into trailing free cash flow is the soft spot. Replacing it with the $2,502M average gives $125,084M, or 0.97x conversion, a 2.5% free-cash-flow yield and 40.2x price to free cash flow on the $5,029.6bn market capitalisation; zeroing the line gives $122,582M and its best clean year $127,306M, so the defensible band is $122.6-127.3B (39.5-41.0x), with $125.1B the midpoint; anything below $122.6B subtracts more than the line contains. The $13,270M of gross intangibles added against investing "other" of $1,780M is consistent with the $13,531M build being deferred consideration — an unpaid purchase, making $123,152M the figure, inside the band. ### Returns clear the cost of capital several times; the multiple does not clear the risk

ROE of 148.8% and ROA of 36.1% are genuine, and the reported ROIC of 320.6% is an artefact of $146.5B of cash and negative working capital that shrink invested capital to $45,347M. The measure that survives is cash return on book capital: normalised free cash flow of $125.1B over equity plus debt of $191,864M, or 65.2%, against 57.3% in FY2025. With the ten-year Treasury at 4.93% and an equity risk premium of 4.5-5.5%, a 9-11% cost of equity is cleared several times; the price is the constraint: $5,029.6bn of market capitalisation on 14,594.18M shares outstanding at 17 July 2026 is 39.0x trailing net income of $128,930M, a 2.6% earnings yield; the $5,072B figure uses the June quarter's 14,715M diluted weighted-average count, 39.3x. Capital allocation agrees: nine-month buybacks of $62,094M plus dividends of $11,778M are 67.0% of reported free cash flow and 72.4% of the $102,057M normalised figure, net cash rose, and shares fell 1.7% while net income rose 20.0%, so buybacks added 2.4 points of the 22.4% EPS growth. Not a debt-funded buyback story. [S6, S7, S10]

### What the next print has to clear

No audited fiscal 2026 exists: Apple reports the September quarter on 2 November 2026. Guidance is 9-11% revenue growth for the quarter ($111.7-113.7B off $102.5B), iPhone mid-teens; the register's only consensus is iPhone revenue, $252.4B for FY2026 (+20.4% on the $209,586M filed for FY2025) and $277.4B for FY2027 (+9.9%), with no group-revenue consensus held. On trailing figures at a 17.3% tax rate: 200 basis points of gross margin is $0.52 of EPS (6.0%), 500 basis points is $1.31 (15.0%), losing the $20B search payment is $1.12 (12.9%) and a 10% fall in iPhone revenue at 39.9% is $0.55 (6.3%). Gross margin moves the outcome most because it applies to all $466,823M of revenue while a unit miss applies only to hardware. For the investor, earnings quality is not the constraint; the price is. The open diligence: December-quarter gross margin guidance, FY2027 memory contracted at fixed prices, what the $12,116M of net intangibles bought, and what sits in the $13,531M rise in other non-current liabilities. [S71, S72]

arguments.markdown:
Apple's moat is real but uneven: in-house silicon, operating-system control and a 2.5-billion-device installed base are hard to replicate, while the intelligence layer this cycle sells on is rented from Google, so AI protects the franchise without widening it. iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, announced on 2026-09-09 and on sale from 2026-09-18, start at $1,199 and $1,299, ship the 2nm A20 Pro and run iOS 27 with Siri rebuilt on Gemini; iPhone net sales were $54.25bn in the quarter to 2026-06-27, up 22%, while R&D rose 33% to $34.04bn over nine months as capex fell. [S113, S6]

### The hardware cycle is being re-priced, not matured

Apple split its launch: the Pro, Pro Max and the first foldable, iPhone Duo, arrived in September 2026; the standard iPhone 18, 18e and Air 2 are reported for spring 2027, and the iPhone 17 was cut to $899. Selling the 2nm-constrained models into the holiday quarter and the volume models in March turns one spike into two, and the A20 Pro's move to 2nm from the A19's 3nm plus the in-house C2 modem are the parts of the stack Apple still owns end to end. At a fixed price a node advantage becomes margin or performance, and insourcing the modem removes a royalty and gives control of cellular power and cost. The offset is memory: the June 2026 filing expects semiconductor, NAND and DRAM constraints to intensify, and products gross margin already leans on tariff refunds that will not recur. Prices rose into that memory-cost cycle, and the December 2026 quarter is the first test. [S112, S6]

| Dimension | Apple | Google | Samsung | Huawei | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Silicon | In-house A-series, 2nm | In-house Tensor | External suppliers | In-house Kirin | S113, S112 |
| Frontier model | Licensed Gemini | Owns Gemini | Licenses Google | In-house stack | S111 |
| AI compute | Rented Google TPUs | Own TPUs and datacentres | Rents cloud | Domestic cloud | S118 |
| AI organisation | Under Software Engineering since 2025-12-01 | DeepMind | Own research | Own research | S127 |

### Siri shipped, two years late and in beta

Siri AI went out with iOS 27 on 2026-09-14 as an English beta, five more languages promised for October — 23 months after Apple Intelligence shipped in October 2024, and after the personalised-Siri promise slipped in 2025. The assistant underneath is a multi-year Google Gemini deal confirmed on 2026-01-12, reported by Bloomberg at a 1.2-trillion-parameter model and $1bn a year; neither confirmed the price. Apple contributes the interface, personal context, camera input and Private Cloud Compute. Ownership moved first: on 2025-12-01 Foundation Models, ML research and AI safety passed to software chief Craig Federighi, with Amar Subramanya as VP of AI, as John Giannandrea stepped down ahead of retirement. Apple bought what it could not ship. [S111, S122, S127]

::: evidence
**The flagship AI feature runs on a competitor's frontier model and a competitor's chips.** Google confirmed on 2026-01-12 a multi-year deal to supply Gemini for the rebuilt Siri, reported at $1bn a year, while Apple's own foundation models were trained on 8,192 Google TPU v4 and 2,048 TPU v5p chips rented through Google Cloud. Apple keeps the interface; not the model or the compute. [S111, S118]
:::

### The licence is small per device and dangerous per query

At the reported $1bn a year the Gemini licence is 0.65% of the $154,859M trailing operating income and $0.06 of EPS, below the $0.52 that 200 basis points of gross margin are worth. Across the 2.5 billion active devices Apple disclosed on 2026-01-29, $0.50, $1 and $2 per device a year cost $1.25bn, $2.5bn and $5.0bn, taking EPS to $0.07, $0.14 and $0.28; booked as a service they would cut services gross margin from 76.3% to 75.3%, 74.2% and 72.2%. The $1bn implies $0.40 a device. Apple does not disclose the classification; R&D up 33% on "infrastructure-related costs, including investments in artificial intelligence" while capex fell points to R&D, and the choice changes the margin narrative, not EPS. The tail is per-query pricing: at an assumed 1 billion queries a day each cent is $3.65bn a year; Apple discloses neither volume nor rate. [S6, S111, S152]

| Per-device price | Annual cost at 2.5bn devices | vs reported $1bn | Services gross margin if booked there | EPS impact | Share of TTM operating income | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $0.40, implied by $1bn | $1.00bn | — | 75.5% | $0.06 | 0.65% | S111, S152, S6 |
| $0.50 | $1.25bn | +25% | 75.3% | $0.07 | 0.81% | S6, S152 |
| $1.00 | $2.50bn | 2.5x | 74.2% | $0.14 | 1.61% | S6, S152 |
| $2.00 | $5.00bn | 5.0x | 72.2% | $0.28 | 3.23% | S6, S152 |

| Metric | Value | Method | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| A20 Pro process node | 2nm (A19: 3nm) | Apple launch specification | S113, S112 |
| Siri AI availability | English beta from 2026-09-14 | Apple release | S113 |
| Active installed base | More than 2.5bn devices | Company release, 2026-01-29 | S152 |
| R&D, nine months to 2026-06-27 | $34.04bn, +33% | 10-Q | S6 |
| Capex, nine months to 2026-06-27 | $6.80bn (prior year $9.47bn) | 10-Q cash-flow statement | S6 |

### Where the moat actually sits

| Barrier | Difficulty (1-10) | Why | Time to replicate | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Silicon design and process access | 8 | Custom SoC, 2nm allocation, modem integration | 4-6 years | S113, S112 |
| OS and installed-base switching costs | 9 | Continuity, App Store, 76.3% services margin | 7+ years | S6, S152 |
| Manufacturing process know-how | 6 | AI-matched hinge, confocal scanning, printed layers | 3-4 years | S114 |
| Frontier AI model | 3 | Bought from Google, no frontier training at scale | 1-2 years, by licence | S111, S118 |
| Developer and services ecosystem | 8 | $91.73bn nine-month services revenue, defaults under pressure | 5+ years | S6 |
| **Composite moat** | **Strong hardware, weak AI** | Hardware barrier real, intelligence barrier rented | Years on hardware | S113, S6 |

The replication test favours hardware: a funded team of fifty with every published patent could match a Duo-class hinge in a few years and an A-series-class chip only after a full node cycle, and would still lack the installed base; the assistant can be licensed, as Apple did.

### Wearables, health and Vision are optionality, not a second engine

Health is the most credible adjacency: hypertension notifications on Apple Watch carry FDA clearance and peer-reviewed scrutiny in *Hypertension*, which questions their accuracy; a monthly alert is not a measurement, so the claim is narrow. Vision Pro sits inside Wearables with no disclosed revenue and no confirmed successor. Both add upgrade reasons and are sold as features, not platforms with their own economics. [S124, S5]

| Product | Stage | Launch | Revenue or share | Margin | Next milestone | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| iPhone 18 Pro / Pro Max | Shipping | 2026-09-18 | iPhone $54.25bn in Q3 FY2026, +22% | Not disclosed by model | December 2026 mix | S113, S6 |
| iPhone Duo (foldable) | Shipping | Announced 2026-09-09 | Not disclosed | Not disclosed | Durability and returns | S114 |
| Services | Shipping | Ongoing | $91.73bn in nine months, +14% | 76.3% | DMA compliance | S6 |
| Wearables and Vision Pro | Shipping | Watch Series 11, Ultra 3, SE 3 (FY2025) | Not separately disclosed | Not disclosed | Health-feature adoption | S5, S124 |

### The patent position is broad, thinning and hard to verify

The portfolio is broad rather than anchored in one blocking family, and it thinned in 2025, when Apple slipped down the U.S. ranking (table below). No individual patent number is cited because none could be verified against a USPTO record; freedom-to-operate risk sits in foldable hinges, displays and health sensing, where verification matters most.

| Patent or portfolio | Area | Jurisdiction | Filed | Granted | Status | Relevance | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| U.S. utility grants, 2025 | Silicon, RF, display, health | US | — | 2,722 grants (2024: 3,082; rank 7th) | Granted, down 12% | Breadth, no blocking family | S117 |
| Foldable hinge and display assemblies | Hinge, crease, lamination | US, CN, EU (reported) | Not disclosed | Not disclosed | Pending and granted, unverified | Duo durability | S114 |
| On-device inference efficiency | Routing, model compression | Not verified | — | — | Published research, no patent number | Inference cost | S52, S53 |

If Siri AI leaves beta with usage data showing its integration beats standalone assistants, the layer is worth more than a licensed feature; silence after 2026-11-02 confirms this reading. If the Gemini term is a bridge to its own model, the dependency is temporary. Until then the technology case rests on silicon, yield and switching costs, and the AI case rests on distribution. Confidence is high on machine facts, medium on model economics, low on patents.
