sources.title: TrendForce: Memory 1Q26 price surge — Samsung memory ASP +146%, SK hynix DRAM ASP +mid-60% q/q
sources.claims: Samsung average memory ASP (DRAM+NAND) rose ~146% in 1Q26 versus the 2025 full-year average; SK hynix DRAM ASP +mid-60% q/q and NAND ASP +mid-70% q/q; Samsung mobile memory costs for its DX division rose ~107% versus the prior-year average; mobile memory reached 9.4% of Samsung DX procurement mix in 1Q26.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens any assumption that Apple's 39.9% products gross margin (9M FY2026) is durable: component cost inflation is running at triple-digit percentages and Apple names memory as a cost headwind in its Q3 FY2026 10-Q.

sources.title: Ninth Circuit opinion, Epic Games v. Apple, No. 25-2935 (2025-12-11): 27% link-out commission had prohibitive effect
sources.claims: The Ninth Circuit held that Apple's 27% commission on purchases made after a user follows a link out of an app had a prohibitive effect and violated the 2021 injunction, and remanded for the district court to decide what commission, if any, Apple may charge on such purchases.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the assumption that App Store take rates (15-30% in-app, 27% link-out) are intact: the link-out commission is unenforceable pending remand, so developers of large digital-goods apps can move payments outside the 15-30% structure.

sources.title: 9to5Mac: Google defends its Safari deal with Apple in antitrust appeal — 36% of Safari search ad revenue, ~$20bn paid in 2022
sources.claims: Court records in the Google search antitrust case show Apple received 36% of search advertising revenue generated through Safari and that Google paid Apple about $20bn in 2022; Judge Mehta's remedy lets Google keep paying Apple for Safari default placement but bans exclusivity and caps any default arrangement at 12 months, giving rivals an annual shot at the placement; Google appealed to the D.C. Circuit on 2026-05-22 seeking reversal in full; Eddy Cue testified Microsoft offered 100% of search ad revenue and Apple still judged Bing less profitable.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the view that the Google payment is a stable annuity: the 12-month default limit converts a multi-year exclusive into an annually re-bid contract, so the ~$20bn (2022) stream is repriced by negotiation and by rivals' willingness to bid.

sources.title: S&P Global Market Intelligence: Apple earnings preview Q4 2026 — consensus iPhone $56.4bn quarter, $252.4bn FY2026, $277.4bn FY2027
sources.claims: Consensus expects Apple's September 2026 quarter to deliver $56.4bn of iPhone revenue, $252.4bn for fiscal 2026 and $277.4bn for fiscal 2027; the preview flags supply-chain questions and whether Apple can meet upgrade demand plus the Duo foldable in the March 2027 quarter.
sources.claims_weakened: Sets the bar the 2026-11-02 print must clear: consensus iPhone growth of ~20% for FY2026 leaves little room if memory supply constrains the December quarter. Page body returned HTTP 403; figures taken from the indexed summary.

sources.title: MacRumors: Apple to report Q4 FY2026 on November 2, 2026 — guidance +9-11% revenue, iPhone mid-teens
sources.claims: Apple's fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter results will be published on 2026-11-02 (call 2:00 p.m. PT) with new CEO John Ternus and CFO Kevan Parekh; on the Q3 FY2026 call CFO Parekh guided September-quarter total revenue to grow 9-11% y/y and iPhone revenue to grow mid-teens with FX headwinds and supply constraints; Q4 FY2025 revenue was $102.5bn, implying $111.7-113.7bn; iPhone Duo foldable launches 2026-10-23 and falls in Q1 FY2027; iPhone 18 Pro launched 2026-09-18; Apple Watch Series 12, Ultra 4 and AirPods 5 shipped in the quarter.
sources.claims_weakened: Establishes that no audited FY2026 full-year statements exist as of 2026-10-31, so any FY2026 annual figure is a nine-month or trailing-twelve-month construction.

sources.title: MacRumors: Apple reaches 2.5 billion active devices (Q1 FY2026, 2026-01-29)
sources.claims: Apple said its installed base passed 2.5 billion active devices in the quarter ended December 2025 (Q1 FY2026), with the increase reported at about 150 million devices since 2025.
sources.claims_weakened: The 2.5 billion figure is a company statement made on an earnings call, not a filed disclosure; Apple's 10-K and 10-Q do not quantify the installed base, so per-device metrics built on it are estimates.

sources.title: Seeking Alpha: Apple Q4 2026 earnings preview — FY2026 iPhone units estimated at 261 million
sources.claims: FY2026 iPhone unit estimates were revised up to 261 million from 258 million since the previous quarter; Apple stock rose 18.4% since May 2026 and 27.5% year to date.
sources.claims_weakened: Unit estimates are third-party and paywalled; Apple has not disclosed iPhone unit sales since FY2019, so any per-unit economics rest on sell-side estimates.

sources.title: Samsung Electronics third quarter 2026 results (KRW 195.3tn revenue, KRW 107.4tn operating profit)
sources.claims: Q3 2026 revenue KRW 195.3tn (+14% q/q) and operating profit KRW 107.4tn; DS (semiconductor) division revenue KRW 147.1tn and operating profit KRW 106.5tn; DX (devices/mobile) division posted an operating loss of KRW 0.8tn; memory prices rose across all applications on server demand; memory business expects 2027 AI-driven demand to exceed industry supply and Q4 2026 demand growth to continue.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the view that the memory cost cycle peaks in 2026: the supplier expects 2027 demand above supply, so Apple's handset bill of materials keeps rising into FY2027 and its device gross-margin guidance must absorb it.

sources.title: 9to5Mac — Apple's search deal with Google could face renewed scrutiny as DOJ appeals antitrust ruling
sources.claims: Judge Mehta's final judgment of 2025-12-05 preserved Google's ability to pay Apple for non-exclusive default placement, capped default deals at 12 months and barred exclusivity; the DOJ and states cross-appealed in February 2026, so a payment ban remains possible on appeal.
sources.claims_weakened: The remedy did not ban payments, contrary to some secondary reports claiming a 2026 default-payment ban took effect.

sources.title: Apple Newsroom — Apple announces changes for apps in the European Union
sources.claims: From 2026-10-01 Apple's unified EU terms set 26% commission on App Store in-app purchase, 20% on alternative payment processing, 15% on link-outs, and a 5% Core Technology Commission for apps distributed via alternative marketplaces or the web; Apple says the changes resolve disagreements with the Commission.
sources.claims_weakened: Developer groups called the terms unacceptable, so the EU settlement may not be durable; Apple's EU App Store revenue is not disclosed to size the impact.

sources.title: European Commission — Commission finds Apple and Meta in breach of the Digital Markets Act (IP/25/1085)
sources.claims: European Commission found Apple breached the DMA anti-steering obligation and fined it EUR 500 million on 2025-04-23; Meta fined EUR 200 million in the same decision package.
sources.claims_weakened: The fine equals about 0.1% of Apple's FY2025 net sales, so the business-model remedies matter more than the penalty.

sources.title: Cravath — Epic Games' Ninth Circuit win affirming civil contempt finding
sources.claims: Ninth Circuit affirmed the civil contempt finding against Apple on 2025-12-11 for willful violation of the anti-steering injunction; it held Apple may charge only limited fees on linked transactions tied to the cost of services it provides, and affirmed the steering injunction.
sources.claims_weakened: Apple's ability to charge any commission on external purchases in the US is now constrained, reducing App Store take-rate control independent of the DOJ case.

sources.title: Stratrix — Why Google pays Apple $20 billion a year for default search
sources.claims: Google paid Apple about $20 billion in 2022 for Safari default search placement, equal to 36% of Google's Safari search revenue, per the US v. Google trial record; Judge Mehta's 2024 liability ruling made the payments central evidence.
sources.claims_weakened: Apple does not disclose the payment, so the current amount and margin are unverified; the 2022 trial figure may overstate or understate today's run rate.

sources.title: U.S. and Plaintiff States v. Apple Inc. — DOJ Antitrust Division case page
sources.claims: DOJ and 16 states/DC filed a civil monopolization case against Apple on 2024-03-21 in the District of New Jersey; DOJ seeks equitable relief, not damages.
sources.claims_weakened: Apple's 10-K says it has substantial defenses; no ruling on the merits has been issued.

sources.title: Ashurst — EU General Court rejects Apple challenges to European Commission DMA designation decisions
sources.claims: On 2026-07-08 the EU General Court dismissed Apple's challenges to its DMA gatekeeper designation for the App Store, iOS and Safari; the substance of Apple's Article 6(7) interoperability challenge is unresolved and a first-instance ruling is unlikely before late 2027, so Apple must comply meanwhile.
sources.claims_weakened: Apple's DMA appeal therefore offers little near-term relief from interoperability obligations.

sources.title: Apple Newsroom: App Store ecosystem reaches record $1.4 trillion
sources.claims: Apple-commissioned study: App Store ecosystem facilitated ~$1.4T of developer billings and sales in 2025, up from ~$1.3T in 2024; physical goods and services ~$1.1T, in-app advertising ~$151B, digital goods and services ~$149B; 850M average weekly visitors across 175 countries. Company-provided and not independently audited.
sources.claims_weakened: The $1.4T figure measures gross ecosystem commerce, not Apple revenue; only the ~$149B digital-goods slice is commissionable, so it overstates the services revenue pool if read as TAM.

sources.title: IDC: Smartphone Shipments Set for Record 16.7% Drop in 2026, as the Memory Crisis Hits Full Force
sources.claims: 2026 global smartphone shipments -16.7% to just over 1.0B units, steepest annual contraction on record; total market value +6.3% to $613B; ASP $581 (+27.6%); NAND/DRAM costs up >300% YoY; Android -24.3%, share down 7pp; iOS shipments -1.3%, share up ~4pp to record 23.6%; HarmonyOS nearly triples to 51M units; Apple foldable entry H2 2026, >17M foldable iPhones by 2027, ~40% of foldables, ASP >$2,550, >$45.7B value; memory supply stabilises 2028.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens any assumption of unit-led market growth to 2030: the market is shrinking in units while growing in value, and Apple's near-term growth depends on price/mix and a new foldable category, not market volume.

sources.title: IDC Worldwide Wearable Device Tracker: Q2 2026 results and 2026-2030 forecast
sources.claims: Wearable shipments ~148M units in Q2 2026, +2.7% YoY; Apple 15.5% share (+8.9%), Xiaomi 11.7% (-6.6%), Huawei 10.9% (+8.4%), Samsung 6.8% (-2.9%). Apple leads earwear with 17.2%; Huawei leads smartwatches 18.8% vs Apple 17.2%. 2026 forecast ~625M units (+1.7%), 2.4% CAGR 2026-2030 to ~687M units; smartwatches -3.7% in 2026; glasses +35.2% in 2026, 18.1% CAGR.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens a wearables recovery story: smartwatches shrink in 2026 and Apple's overall wearables share (15.5%) is below its 2025 peak quarters (21.0% in Q4 2025).

sources.title: Huawei 2025 Annual Report press release
sources.claims: Huawei 2025 revenue CNY880.9B, net profit CNY68B, R&D CNY192.3B (21.8% of revenue), audited by KPMG; consumer business "worked to overcome formidable challenges" and drove the HarmonyOS ecosystem; closing rate USD1 = CNY6.9906.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the view that US export controls have neutralised Huawei as a premium competitor: it still funds R&D at ~22% of revenue and grew smartphone share in China in 2026.

sources.title: IDC: Why Huawei and Apple Grew While China's Smartphone Market Fell Again in Q2 2026
sources.claims: China smartphone shipments ~66M units in Q2 2026, -4.3% YoY, fifth straight decline; H1 2026 ~134M units, -4.2%. Vendor shares Q2 2026: Huawei 22.6% (+19.4% YoY), Apple 18.1% (+24.4%), OPPO 16.0%, vivo 16.0%, Xiaomi 12.4% (-21.7%), Honor 11.3%. Top six ~96% of market. IDC expects China decline to widen to ~20% in H2 2026 and recovery around 2028-2029. Apple and Huawei held prices while Android vendors raised them; Apple's signalling of H2 price increases pulled demand forward.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the view that Apple's China revenue growth (+30% 9M FY2026) is a durable share recovery: it coincides with a shrinking market, price-increase pull-forward and Huawei at a five-year share high.

sources.title: TWICE reporting Omdia: average smartphone price to reach $565 in 2026
sources.claims: Omdia: global smartphone ASP forecast to rise from $467 in 2025 to $565 in 2026, +21% (+$98), the largest annual increase on record; DRAM and NAND prices up more than 80% in Q1 2026; vendors prioritising value over volume.

sources.title: The Desk reporting WARC: global ad spending forecast $1.34 trillion in 2026
sources.claims: WARC Media: global advertising spend forecast to grow 11.9% to $1.34T in 2026, after 10% growth in both 2024 and 2025; social media advertising +21.3% to $394.6B; VOD/streaming ad spending +15.1%.

sources.title: China Biz Insider: Xiaomi Q2 2026 results, memory squeezes phones
sources.claims: Xiaomi Q2 2026: group revenue RMB108.9B; smartphone shipments 31.2M units, 11.5% global share; smartphone gross margin 8.5% as memory costs rose 78-83%; adjusted net profit -42.6% YoY.

sources.title: FoneArena reporting Samsung Q3 2026 results: mobile loss despite revenue growth
sources.claims: Samsung Electronics Q3 2026: MX and Networks revenue KRW37.7T (+10.55% YoY, +13.55% QoQ), operating loss KRW0.6T, second consecutive quarterly loss despite 11% higher smartphone revenue; group profit driven by record memory earnings; flagship and foldable launches supported mobile revenue.

sources.title: Counterpoint Research: Global smartphone shipments grew 2% YoY in 2025
sources.claims: Counterpoint Research: global smartphone shipments grew 2% YoY in 2025; Apple led with 20% share and 10% YoY growth, the highest among the top five; Samsung grew 5% with 19% share; Xiaomi third but Q4 2025 shipments -11% YoY. Methodology: Market Monitor OEM shipment by region, published August 2026.

sources.title: 9to5Mac: Spotify crosses 300 million paid subscribers as Apple Music readies iOS 27
sources.claims: Spotify crossed 300 million paying subscribers (August 2026), after 293M Premium subscribers and 761M MAU at Q1 2026 (Spotify disclosure, 2026-04-28); Apple Music estimated at ~100-108M subscribers by MIDiA and other analysts.

sources.title: AppleInsider reporting Counterpoint: Apple holds 65% of premium smartphone market, H1 2026
sources.claims: Counterpoint Research Handset Model Sales Tracker (wholesale ASP >= $600): premium segment unit sales +5% YoY in H1 2026; premium share of global smartphone sales 29% in H1 2026 vs 25% H1 2025 and 20% H1 2022 (record); Apple 65% of global premium unit sales in H1 2026, +9% YoY, driven by iPhone 17 lineup.

sources.title: 9to5Mac reporting IDC: Apple grows Mac shipments as broader PC market declines (Q2 2026)
sources.claims: IDC PC Tracker Q2 2026: global PC shipments 68.2M units, -4.9% YoY, first decline since 2024; Lenovo 24.4% share, HP 19.1%, Dell 13.6%, Apple 9.9% (+10.1% shipments, only major vendor with significant growth, helped by MacBook Neo launch), ASUS 7.4%. IDC: units falling while revenue climbs because vendors push price increases faster than demand falls; no inventory pull-forward expected in H2 2026; memory shortage not easing until early 2028.

sources.title: Counterpoint via TelecomLead: China smartphone shipments -10% YoY in Q3 2026; Huawei 21.3% share, Apple 19.5% (+4.8pp); iPhone 18 Pro launch sales +23.5%
sources.claims: China smartphone market contracted 10% YoY in Q3 2026 (Counterpoint); Huawei 21.3% shipment share vs Apple 19.5%, Apple up 4.8pp from 14.7%; iPhone 18 Pro first-three-week sales +23.5% vs iPhone 17 Pro launch; standard iPhone 18 launch moved to 2027; Omdia estimates market -12% to 59.3m units with Apple 11.6m.
sources.claims_weakened: The framing that Apple is losing China share to Huawei; the assumption that iPhone volume growth is broad-based rather than Pro-mix driven.

sources.title: FinanceCharts: Apple P/E 39.52x trailing and 35.21x forward as of 2026-10-30, 12-month average 35.66x
sources.claims: AAPL trailing P/E 39.52x and forward P/E 35.21x at the 2026-10-30 close; trailing P/E 10.82% above its 12-month average of 35.66x.
sources.claims_weakened: Any claim that the multiple is at or below its own recent average, or that valuation offers a margin of safety.

sources.title: Apple Newsroom: Tim Cook to become Executive Chairman, John Ternus CEO effective 2026-09-01
sources.claims: Board unanimously approved Tim Cook moving to executive chairman and John Ternus, SVP Hardware Engineering, becoming CEO effective 2026-09-01.
sources.claims_weakened: Continuity assumptions: the first earnings call under a new CEO is 2026-11-02, with margin and AI strategy questions open.

sources.title: TrendForce: iPhone 18 Pro 256GB BOM cost +38% YoY, memory ~34% of BOM in 3Q26 vs ~10% a year earlier
sources.claims: 512GB-class iPhone 18 Pro 256GB bill of materials up ~38% YoY; memory share of BOM rose from ~10% to ~34% in 3Q26 and expected above 40% in 1H27; memory prices up five- to sevenfold since start-2025; Apple likely to sacrifice gross margin to limit price increases; global smartphone production under pressure 2H26-2027.
sources.claims_weakened: The assumption that Apple can hold ~47-48% gross margin through the iPhone 18 cycle; the view that component cost inflation is a one-quarter issue.

sources.title: CRS Legal Sidebar LSB11362: Federal court endorses behavioral remedies, rejects structural relief in Google search case
sources.claims: Congressional Research Service analysis of the Google search remedies ruling: the court endorsed behavioural remedies and rejected structural relief; under a broad payment ban, distribution partners would face a choice between placing Google Search as default without payment or entering less lucrative deals.
sources.claims_weakened: Claims that the judgment broke up Google or banned all default-search payments.

sources.title: Hughes Hubbard: Court issues remedies ruling in United States v. Google Search case — exclusivity barred, payments not banned
sources.claims: In the September 2025 remedies ruling in United States v. Google, the court did not ban Google's payments to distribution partners such as Apple for default search placement; it prohibited exclusive search distribution agreements, required sharing of search index and syndication data at marginal cost, and declined structural relief.
sources.claims_weakened: Secondary commentary claiming the remedy banned Google's ~$20bn annual payments to Apple, or that it imposed search choice screens.

sources.title: TechCrunch: Apple overhauls its EU App Store fees, loosens rules for alternative app stores
sources.claims: Apple overhauled EU App Store fees in August 2026 to resolve its DMA dispute: it had been fined EUR500 million for non-compliance in 2025 and faced further penalties; the new terms replace the Core Technology Fee with a 5% Core Technology Commission and set commission rates for alternative payments and link-outs.

sources.title: Apple, Google strike Gemini deal for revamped Siri (Reuters, 2026-01-12)
sources.claims: Apple will use Google's Gemini models for its revamped Siri under a multi-year deal; Google confirmed a multiyear AI deal to power Apple's AI technology including Siri (headline and snippet retrieved; article body behind a paywall/login).
sources.claims_weakened: Undermines the claim that Apple's AI stack is fully in-house; shows the flagship assistant depends on a competitor's frontier model.

sources.title: iPhone 18: Rumors and Release Date (MacRumors roundup)
sources.claims: Apple split the iPhone 18 launch: iPhone 18 Pro, 18 Pro Max and the foldable iPhone Duo launched in September 2026; the standard iPhone 18, iPhone 18e and second-generation iPhone Air are expected in spring 2027; A20 built on 2nm versus A19 on 3nm; C2 in-house modem expected across the iPhone 18 line; iPhone 17 repriced to $899 and Macs and iPads repriced in June 2026 amid memory costs.
sources.claims_weakened: Some roadmap items are rumour-based; the launch split and 2nm A20 are consistent with Apple's own September 2026 release.

sources.title: Apple debuts iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max (Apple Newsroom)
sources.claims: iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max announced 2026-09-09, on sale 2026-09-18, from $1,199 and $1,299; A20 Pro chip; iOS 27 with Apple Intelligence; Siri AI rolling out as a beta on 2026-09-14 in English with French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish in October; features include personal context, onscreen awareness, Camera Siri mode; Private Cloud Compute for cloud processing.
sources.claims_weakened: Qualifies the 'Apple is behind in AI' claim: the Siri overhaul did ship, but as an English-language beta in September 2026, roughly two years after Apple Intelligence launched.

sources.title: The hinge for Apple's new foldable phone was built with AI (TechCrunch)
sources.claims: Apple announced the foldable iPhone Duo at its "Surprise and Shine" event on 2026-09-09; the hinge is manufactured with AI algorithms matching each hinge to its housing, confocal laser scanning and 3D printing of up to 25 photopolymer micro-layers; custom nano-texture finish; quoted Johny Srouji as chief hardware officer; durability of foldables remains unproven in the field.
sources.claims_weakened: Shows manufacturing process know-how as a moat; also shows the foldable's durability and yield are unproven, so the launch is a test rather than a proven franchise.

sources.title: Apple now makes about 25% of iPhones in India after China pivot (Bloomberg via Economic Times)
sources.claims: Apple assembled about 55 million iPhones in India in 2025, up from 36 million in 2024 (+53%), about a quarter of the 220-230 million iPhones made globally; all iPhone 17 models including Pro and Pro Max are assembled in India; Indian assembly and components still cost more than in China or Vietnam; smartphone production subsidies expire 2026-03-31; Apple's India sales passed $9 billion and Apple Pay was to launch in India in 2026.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the "China concentration" risk narrative, but shows India is a costlier, subsidy-dependent base rather than a margin tailwind.

sources.title: What to expect from Apple Q4 2026 financial report (AppleInsider)
sources.claims: Apple's fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter results call is scheduled for 2026-11-02; at Q3 FY2026 Apple guided fourth-quarter revenue growth of 9-11% year over year against analyst expectations of about 12.1% at the time.
sources.claims_weakened: Sets a dated, checkable milestone: FY2026 Q4 results on 2026-11-02, which will show whether the iPhone 18/Duo launch sustained the 22% iPhone growth seen in Q3.

sources.title: Apple drops to 7th in U.S. patent rankings for 2025 as grants fall (9to5Mac, citing IFI CLAIMS)
sources.claims: IFI CLAIMS data: Apple received 2,722 U.S. patent grants in 2025, down from 3,082 in 2024 (about -12%), and fell to 7th place in the U.S. patent ranking; U.S. patent activity declined industry-wide.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the claim that Apple's patent portfolio is deepening; grant counts fell 12% in 2025.

sources.title: Apple to use Google's TPUs for AI instead of Nvidia GPUs (DatacenterDynamics)
sources.claims: Apple trained its foundation models on Google TPUs rather than Nvidia GPUs: 8,192 TPU v4 chips for the AFM-server model and 2,048 TPU v5p chips for the on-device model, accessed through Google Cloud.
sources.claims_weakened: Undercuts any claim that Apple controls its AI training stack; training compute is rented from a rival that now also supplies the Siri model.

sources.title: Apple keeps challenging its interoperability obligations under the DMA (FSFE)
sources.claims: As of 2026-03-22 Apple had received 56 interoperability requests under Article 6(7) of the DMA since May 2025, closing 43, of which 27 closures were fully confidential; Apple continues to challenge its interoperability obligations.
sources.claims_weakened: Shows DMA compliance is an operating cost and a source of feature delay in the EU, not a one-off legal event.

sources.title: GSMArena: Samsung and Apple gain share in a Q3 2026 smartphone market down 20%
sources.claims: Q3 2026 global smartphone market: Samsung led with 23% share (19% a year earlier), Apple second with 22% (18% in Q3 2025), in a market that fell 20% YoY.

sources.title: AI execs and researchers who left Apple, mostly for Meta (Business Insider)
sources.claims: Apple lost AI executives and researchers through 2025, mostly to Meta, which offered large packages; the list of departures spans Siri and foundation-model leadership.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the "talent moat" leg of the AI argument: the teams that built Apple Intelligence were depleted during 2025, just as the Siri rebuild slipped.

sources.title: Apple to use Google's AI model to run new Siri, Bloomberg reports (Reuters)
sources.claims: Bloomberg reported on 2025-11-05 that Apple planned to use a 1.2-trillion-parameter Google Gemini model to help power the Siri revamp, two months before the deal was confirmed.
sources.claims_weakened: Gives the model scale (1.2 trillion parameters), far above any on-device model Apple publishes, which supports the view that the hardest Siri tasks are outsourced.

sources.title: Apple (AAPL) revenue history (Stock Analysis)
sources.claims: Apple revenue was $109.42 billion in the quarter ended 2026-06-27, up 16.36% year over year, taking trailing-twelve-month revenue to $466.82 billion; fiscal 2025 revenue was $416.16 billion (+6.43%).
sources.claims_weakened: Consistent with the 10-Q; shows growth reaccelerated to mid-teens in FY2026 after 6.4% in FY2025.

sources.title: Apple Watch for Hypertension Screening (Hypertension, AHA/ASA, 2026)
sources.claims: Peer-reviewed commentary in Hypertension (AHA/ASA), DOI 10.1161/HYPERTENSIONAHA.125.26031, 2026, treats the FDA clearance of Apple Watch's Hypertension Notification Feature as a juncture for cuffless blood-pressure screening and questions whether notifications are accurate and useful; the Apple Watch is described as the most widely adopted consumer health device globally. Feature is a 30-day chronic-signal notification, not a blood-pressure measurement.
sources.claims_weakened: Tempering: the clinical value of the health features is still contested and the feature informs rather than diagnoses, so health is a differentiation lever, not yet a regulated-therapy business.

sources.title: Alphabet Inc. DEF 14A for the meeting of 2026-06-05
sources.claims: DEF 14A text: Compensation discussion and analysis (found by its heading), paragraphs mentioning Pichai, Total

sources.title: Computer History Museum, "Apple Timeline: Fifty Years of Innovation"
sources.claims: Dated Apple corporate history: founded 1976-04-01 as a partnership (Jobs, Wozniak, Wayne); incorporated 1977-01-03; Apple II 1977-04-16; IPO 1980-12-12 at $22/share raising over $100m (Morgan Stanley, Hambrecht & Quist); Jobs resigns 1985-09-17; NeXT acquired February 1997 and Jobs becomes CEO June 1997; iPod October 2001; iPhone 2007-06-29; iPad 2010-04-03; iPhone 4S/Siri 2011-10-04.
sources.claims_weakened: Nothing on ownership, share count or post-2011 events; it is a museum timeline, not a filing, so financial figures must come from SEC filings.

sources.title: Apple Newsroom, "John Giannandrea to retire from Apple"
sources.claims: On 2025-12-01 Apple announced John Giannandrea, SVP Machine Learning and AI Strategy, was stepping down to serve as an advisor before retiring in spring 2026; AI researcher Amar Subramanya joined as VP of AI reporting to Craig Federighi, leading Apple Foundation Models, ML research and AI Safety and Evaluation; the balance of Giannandrea's organisation moved to Sabih Khan and Eddy Cue.
sources.claims_weakened: Apple does not disclose why Siri deadlines slipped or how AI accountability is split between Federighi, Khan and Cue, so the reorganisation's effectiveness cannot be verified from this release.

sources.title: Apple Newsroom, "Apple announces executive transitions"
sources.claims: On 2025-12-04 Apple announced Jennifer Newstead would become general counsel on 2026-03-01 after joining as SVP in January 2026, succeeding Kate Adams (general counsel since 2017), who retires; also announced Lisa Jackson's retirement.
sources.claims_weakened: Does not state Newstead's prior employer, her pay, or who fills Jackson's environmental policy role.

sources.title: CNBC, "Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella's total comp rises to $96.5 million"
sources.claims: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella's fiscal 2025 total compensation was $96.5 million, up 22% from $79.1 million in fiscal 2024, per Microsoft's proxy filing reported on 2025-10-21.
sources.claims_weakened: Reported figure, not read from the Microsoft proxy itself; the split between salary, cash bonus and stock ($84.2 million) comes from the same reporting and may differ slightly from the summary compensation table.

sources.title: The Daily Pennsylvanian, "Penn alum John Ternus named next Apple CEO"
sources.claims: John Ternus graduated from the University of Pennsylvania in 1997 with a bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering and applied mechanics and a minor in psychology; he was named Apple's next CEO in April 2026 and succeeded Tim Cook on 2026-09-01.
sources.claims_weakened: Student newspaper, so the degree details are not from a registrar; it does not cover his pre-Apple employment.

sources.title: 9to5Mac, "Report: Johny Srouji contemplating leaving Apple"
sources.claims: Reported 2025-12-06: Johny Srouji, Apple's senior vice president of hardware technologies, told Tim Cook he was seriously considering leaving the company in the near future, per a Bloomberg report; the report said he intended to continue his career elsewhere rather than retire.
sources.claims_weakened: Unconfirmed by Apple; no departure has been disclosed, and the report does not say whether he has stayed or been given a new role, so the retention outcome is not publicly disclosed.

sources.title: Apple Inc. 8-K reporting 2025-12-04
sources.claims: 8-K text: Item 5.02 (Departure or Election of Directors and Officers; Compensatory Arrangements)

sources.title: Apple Newsroom: Johny Srouji named Apple's Chief Hardware Officer
sources.claims: Srouji became chief hardware officer effective 2026-04-20, leading Hardware Engineering (Ternus's former remit) and Hardware Technologies; Ternus quoted as incoming CEO. Shows the December 2025 retention risk resolved by promotion, and consolidates silicon plus hardware engineering under one executive.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the claim that Srouji's possible departure remains a live key-person risk; also shows Ternus's hardware bench was filled internally before he became CEO on 2026-09-01.

sources.title: Morningstar/Dow Jones: Apple Waives Age Cap for Two Board Members, Including Chair Levinson
sources.claims: Apple's board waived its age-75 retirement guideline to renominate Chair Art Levinson (75) and Audit Committee Chair Ron Sugar (77) at the 2026 annual meeting, citing their expertise and knowledge of Apple; both are longer-tenured than Cook.
sources.claims_weakened: Qualifies the DEF 14A ages: the two oldest directors were renominated only via a disclosed waiver, so board refreshment is deferred rather than absent.

sources.title: American Antitrust Institute amicus brief in United States v. Google LLC, No. 26-5023 (D.C. Cir.)
sources.claims: The D.C. Circuit appeal is No. 26-5023; the district court's remedy permitted Google to continue paying for default placement while banning exclusivity; the AAI asks the appellate court to prohibit the payment-for-default mechanism, so a payment ban is a live appellate issue, not settled. Google argues the conduct was competition on the merits.
sources.claims_weakened: Any reading that the Google payment is already banned or already safe; it confirms the remedy preserved payments at district court but the ban is sought on appeal, with the decision still ahead.

sources.title: TrendForce: AI server demand sustains memory contract price increases in 4Q26
sources.claims: Conventional DRAM contract prices projected +10-15% QoQ in 4Q26 and NAND Flash +15-20%; mobile DRAM allocations stay tight because capacity shifts to servers; PC OEMs expect DRAM supply to remain tight in 2027 and PC DRAM supply could decline in 2027.
sources.claims_weakened: The view that the memory cost shock is over by the December 2026 quarter or that FY2027 gross margin recovers quickly; price growth moderates but remains positive into 2027.

sources.title: The Antitrust Attorney: Apple's Gemini-Siri deal is the next Microsoft antitrust case (commentary)
sources.claims: X Corp. and xAI sued Apple and OpenAI in the Northern District of Texas on 2025-08-25 over ChatGPT integration and App Store treatment; motions to dismiss were denied on 2025-11-13; discovery closed 2026-05-22; legal commentary argues the Apple-Google Gemini arrangement raises the same default-placement antitrust questions as the search case.
sources.claims_weakened: That Apple's AI distribution deals are outside the antitrust perimeter, and that the regulatory map in the report is complete; a live US suit against Apple over AI integration is not covered by the DOJ, DMA or Google cases.

sources.title: Apple Inc. 8-K reporting 2026-02-24
sources.claims: 8-K text: the whole filing, paragraphs mentioning Say on Pay, say-on-pay, votes, approved

sources.title: Electronics Weekly reporting Counterpoint: China Q3 2026 smartphone shipments -10% YoY, lowest Q3 since 2012; Huawei 21.3%, Apple 19.5%
sources.claims: Counterpoint Q3 2026 China: shipments -10% YoY, lowest Q3 since 2012; Huawei and Apple took 40% of shipments combined, the only top brands to gain share; Huawei 21.3%, Apple 19.5% (second); iPhone 18 Pro series first-three-week sales +23.5% YoY.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the claim that Apple's China competitive position deteriorated on share in Q3 2026; it gained share in a contracting market.

sources.title: wi-fiplanet reporting IDC: China smartphone shipments fell 15.4% in Q3 2026; Apple share 17.8%, Huawei 21.1%
sources.claims: IDC preliminary Q3 2026 China: market -15.4% YoY; Apple 17.8% share (from 15.8%), shipments -4.3%, -15.1% QoQ; Huawei 21.1% share (from 15.2%), shipments +17.3%; Lenovo +1.1%; IDC expects component costs elevated through much of 2027 and continued significant market declines; iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max +$100; iPhone Duo on sale 2026-10-23 at $1,999; standard iPhone 18 held to spring 2027.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens any reading that Apple is losing China share in Q3 2026; it gained share while shipping fewer units. Supports the view that the risk is market contraction and price-led pull-forward, not share loss.

sources.title: MacRumors, "Johny Srouji Taking Over as Apple's Chief Hardware Officer as John Ternus Prepares to Become CEO"
sources.claims: Confirms that Apple announced Johny Srouji as Chief Hardware Officer on 2026-04-20, an expanded role combining Hardware Technologies (his prior remit since 2015) with Hardware Engineering, which John Ternus led before becoming CEO on 2026-09-01. Supports that the December 2025 report of Srouji considering leaving was superseded by promotion rather than departure.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the reading that Apple faced an imminent loss of its silicon chief; leaves open his succession, retention terms and pay, none of which is disclosed in SEC filings.

sources.title: Tickernerd — Apple (AAPL) analyst price targets 2026-2027
sources.claims: 44 covering analysts show a median 12-month price target of $338, with estimates ranging from $245 to $405.
sources.claims_weakened: The dispersion ($245-405) is wide enough that the median target carries little information about intrinsic value; the low end is close to the report's base case.

sources.title: CNBC — Cisco's stock closes at a record for the first time since its dot-com peak in 2000
sources.claims: Cisco closed at $80.25 on 2025-12-10, exceeding its split-adjusted record of $80.06 set on 2000-03-27 — 25 years to recover the dot-com peak.
sources.claims_weakened: Paying a peak multiple for a dominant hardware franchise can cost a quarter-century of price return even when the company keeps compounding; the multiple, not the business, is the risk.

sources.title: TickFlow — Apple (AAPL) stock forecast and price target, October 2026
sources.claims: 50 analysts cover AAPL with a consensus 12-month price target of $339.35, about 1.5% below the $344.63 close on 2026-10-30.
sources.claims_weakened: The sell side sees the shares as fairly valued; a $284 base-case value is far below consensus, so the report's negative price view is genuinely non-consensus.

sources.title: Decision Intel — Nokia collapse case study (2007 peak)
sources.claims: Nokia held 49.4% global mobile-phone share in 2007, reached a peak market capitalisation of about $250bn, and sold its handset business to Microsoft in 2013 for $7.2bn.
sources.claims_weakened: A platform leader at peak share can lose most of its value within six years when the next computing interface changes — the bear case for an Apple that rents its AI layer.

sources.title: Trendonify — S&P 500 forward P/E ratio
sources.claims: The S&P 500 traded at a forward P/E of 18.09 on 2026-10-30 against a five-year median of 20.88, the 5th percentile of that range.
sources.claims_weakened: The market multiple is below its own five-year median, so Apple's 35.2x forward is about 1.9 times the index rather than being flattered by a broadly expensive market.

sources.title: Wikipedia — United States v. Microsoft Corp.
sources.claims: The US antitrust case against Microsoft was filed in 1998; the D.C. Circuit upheld the liability finding in 2001 but rejected the breakup order, and the parties settled in 2001 with conduct remedies.
sources.claims_weakened: It supports the decision rule that platform antitrust usually ends in conduct remedies and years of overhang rather than structural break-up — the base case for United States v. Apple.

sources.title: CNBC — OpenAI told investors it hit roughly $50 billion in annualized revenue at end-September 2026
sources.claims: OpenAI told investors it reached about $50B annualised revenue at end-September 2026 (below the $68B figure widely reported), with 77% total run-rate growth and 107% enterprise run-rate growth in Q3 2026; valuation $852B; prospectus confidentially filed in June 2026 with a possible 2027 IPO.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the $68B revenue figure reported in late September 2026; also shows OpenAI's revenue is about 41% of Apple's $120.5B services revenue, so it is a fast-growing but smaller pool today.

sources.title: The Verge — OpenAI DevDay 2026: biggest news and announcements
sources.claims: ChatGPT had 1.2 billion weekly users at OpenAI DevDay on 2026-09-29, up from 1 billion in July 2026; OpenAI announced a $500-a-month ChatGPT Pro tier alongside $100 and $200 tiers; its Dots agent is restricted to paid Pro tiers; OpenAI is working with Jony Ive on a device to ship no earlier than February 2027.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens any view that AI assistants remain a negligible competitor to Apple's services or that Apple's hardware distribution is a durable moat against assistant-layer rivals.

sources.title: CIRP — iPhone 17 average selling price contributes to record December 2025 quarter (US-WARP $1,077)
sources.claims: US weighted average retail price of new iPhones (US-WARP) was $1,077 in the December 2025 quarter, the highest December quarter since CIRP began its survey, up from $953 a year earlier, after Apple raised iPhone 17 Pro, Pro Max and Air prices by $100 in September 2025; the quarter was Apple's record December quarter.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the claim that a $100 price increase suppresses demand: a full quarter of sales after the iPhone 17 increase produced a record US ASP and a record Apple quarter. It is survey-based, US-only and mix-driven, so it does not by itself establish full-cycle price elasticity.

sources.title: Synergy Research Group — Q2 2026 cloud market $143.4B; AWS 28%, Microsoft 20%, Google 15%
sources.claims: Q2 2026 enterprise cloud infrastructure services spending reached $143.4B, up 43% year on year, the highest growth in eight years; trailing-twelve-month revenue $500B; worldwide share AWS 28%, Microsoft 20%, Google 15%.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the view that Apple can build a services moat independent of cloud scale; shows Microsoft and Google each hold cloud positions Apple lacks.

sources.title: Apple reports first quarter results (Apple Newsroom, 2026-01-29)
sources.claims: Apple's active installed base passed 2.5 billion devices, announced with fiscal 2026 first-quarter results (quarter ended 2025-12-27): revenue $143.8bn, +16% year over year, diluted EPS $2.84, iPhone and Services at all-time records; used as the device denominator for per-device licence sensitivity.
sources.claims_weakened: Company-reported installed base is unaudited and mixes iPhones, iPads, Macs and wearables, so an AI licence priced only on iPhones would spread over a smaller denominator and raise the per-device cost.

sources.title: Stockrow — Apple (AAPL) P/E ratio: ten-year range and percentile
sources.claims: Trailing P/E of 39.8x on 2026-10-22; over the ten years to that date the P/E ranged from 9.9x (January 2016) to 42.5x (December 2024), and the current reading was higher than 99% of that period; above the technology sector median of 28.0x.
sources.claims_weakened: Aggregator, not a primary feed; trailing rather than forward P/E; the page itself returned HTTP 403 on retrieval, so only the search-result summary is cited; price and EPS bases may differ from S7.

scope.decision: Whether Apple (AAPL) belongs on a long-only fund's watchlist, and at what price and with what conditions it becomes an actionable long.

spines.spine: Public equity — earnings quality, competitive position, valuation, catalysts, downside risk
spines.must_answer: Is the market mispricing Apple's future cash flow or its risk? Framed on FY2025/FY2026 revenue growth, services mix, gross margin, FCF conversion, ROIC versus WACC, the multiple versus peers and its own history, the catalyst calendar (iPhone cycle, Apple Intelligence, capital return) and the bear-case drawdown. Answered: the franchise compounds but the price already capitalises a 50.1% peak margin and a 35.2x forward multiple; DCF $212, base $284, probability-weighted $292 against $344.63.

spines.spine: Policy / geopolitics-sensitive — national strategy, export controls, tariffs, platform regulation, market access
spines.must_answer: Does policy create a moat or a hidden constraint? Quantified: the ~$20bn Google default-search payment (18.3% of services revenue, 15% of operating income, a 2022 litigated estimate), the EU 5-26% fee schedule in force 2026-10-01, DOJ v Apple filed 2024-03-21 with no trial date, the Ninth Circuit contempt of 2025-12-11 and Supreme Court certiorari granted 2026-06-30, and tariffs that add two points of gross margin in refunds while memory costs rise.

spines.spine: Consumer / brand — demand durability versus promotion-driven demand
spines.must_answer: Is iPhone and services demand durable? Tested replacement-cycle length, installed-base growth and switching costs, services attach and pricing power, Greater China demand and Huawei, and whether growth is unit-driven or price/mix-driven. Answered: FY2026 growth is price and mix (units down 16.7% in a market up 6.3% in value), iPhone +22.4% in nine months against services +14.1%, and China is a shrinking pool where Apple gained 4.8 points of share.

research_plan.industry_map: Consumer electronics plus digital services. Value chain: in-house silicon and OS design (Apple) → foundry and memory (TSMC and others) → components and displays → contract assembly (Foxconn, Pegatron, Luxshare; China with an India/Vietnam shift) → distribution (carriers, Apple retail, e-commerce) → an installed base of active devices → platform (iOS/macOS/watchOS) → services (App Store, iCloud, advertising, subscriptions, AppleCare, payments). Decisive bottleneck: control of the OS and installed base that converts hardware gross margin into recurring, higher-margin services revenue; that bottleneck is now squeezed by platform regulation (EU DMA, US App Store remedies) and by the AI capability race that determines the next upgrade cycle. Apple sits as the orchestrator: design and platform in-house, manufacturing outsourced, distribution partly owned, services attached to its own base.
research_plan.geo_lens: Material. Map five reporting regions — Americas, Europe, Greater China, Japan, Rest of Asia Pacific — for revenue, margin and growth; map the manufacturing footprint (China, India, Vietnam) and the supplier base (Taiwan, South Korea, Japan, US); map capital markets (Nasdaq listing, USD reporting) and the comparable set (US mega-cap technology plus global handset makers). Greater China is the swing geography for both demand and supply-chain risk: 17.8% of nine-month FY2026 revenue, a market down 10% on Counterpoint and 15.4% on IDC in Q3 2026, with Apple at 19.5% against Huawei's 21.3%.
research_plan.policy_lens: Material. Jurisdictions mapped: United States (tariffs and Section 232 semiconductor/consumer-electronics actions, DOJ antitrust case against Apple, the Google default-search payment, export controls on advanced chips); European Union (Digital Markets Act fee schedule from 2026-10-01 at 5-26%, the EUR500M DMA fine of 2025-04-23, interoperability obligations, the General Court's 2026-07-08 ruling); China (market access, local-content and security rules, Huawei competition, rare-earth and export-control leverage); India (production-linked incentives that expired 2026-03-31, manufacturing shift); United Kingdom (CMA mobile-market investigation). Policy hits both revenue (App Store take rate, default payments) and cost (tariffs, supply-chain relocation, memory).

Apple Investor Relations — earnings releases, prepared remarks, guidance and shareholder returns

gates: Confirm company identity, legal entity, geography, stage, and business model.
Decide whether the geographic market context lens is material; if yes, map home, revenue, expansion, supplier, comparable-company, capital, exit markets and the investor perspective.
Decide whether the policy and geopolitics lens is material; if yes, map jurisdictions and perspective.
Complete the profile requirements before drafting.
Build the source register with source type, date, confidence, claims and a link or file/page reference.
Use visible source IDs such as [S1] as citations in the report.
Complete the evidence matrix for all material sections before drafting.
Run the pre-draft evidence gate and fix failures.
Draft the report from evidence, not from outline memory.
Run the red-team pass and rewrite weak sections.
research_plan.hypothesis: Watchlist, not ownership, at $344.63 on 2026-10-30. Apple is a genuine cash compounder — 0.97x normalised cash conversion on $125.1bn, $62.2bn of net cash, services at 40.3% of gross profit — but the price capitalises a peak margin and a peak multiple: DCF $212 at a 9.0% cost of equity, sum of the parts $177-238, base case $284, probability-weighted value $292. It becomes an actionable long through a staged entry: 0.75-1.0% of the fund at $270, a second tranche at $245, the 5% cap below $225, and a stop-review above $380. The two facts that would change the call are a 46% gross margin and a D.C. Circuit ban on the Google search payment.
research_plan.author: Lead Analyst

items: Use web and data tools for fresh facts whenever a company, market, price, policy, filing, funding, or executive fact may have changed.
For each major section, record targeted search strings, opened sources, source IDs, and why the selected sources are decision-grade rather than merely convenient.
Use the server's checks for deterministic QA, extraction, citation checks and the delivery folder; do not rely on a one-shot narrative draft.
Do not generate repeated filler paragraphs such as per-section original-document priority, citation-anchor blocks, or repeated metric-card copy; each section must contain content-specific analysis.
Before drafting, write a section distinctness plan: the unique decision question, mechanism, comparison set, counter-evidence, and best visual artifact for each section.
For each section, draft one final-report thesis sentence that directly analyzes the company; never copy internal plan labels or rubric language into the report.
Remove repeated visible scaffolds such as "Economic mechanism", "Comparison and benchmark", "Counter-evidence and risk" and "Investor implication"; keep the scaffold internal.
Use a verdict strip, compact decision cards, selected tables, and at most a few KPI strips; do not repeat the same card, grid or dashboard pattern in every section.
Before writing the executive briefing, summarize the non-consensus or consensus view and the exact evidence that changes the decision.
Treat OCR as a pipeline: inventory files, OCR scan- or slide-heavy material, and keep page, slide or table references for every extracted claim.
Check every page holding numbers, TAM, valuation, customers, clinical or regulatory claims, policy claims, financing terms or team credentials before relying on it.
Mark OCR-derived claims low confidence until checked or corroborated; use ranges for OCR-derived financial inputs.
Build a claim verification table for material company-provided claims: verified, partially verified, unverified, contradicted, or not publicly disclosed.
profile_requirements.evidence: Completed across the run. Fresh facts: the team pulled Apple's FY2025 10-K, the 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-27, the 2026 proxy and 8-Ks from SEC EDGAR [S5, S6, S11, S56], timestamped market data at $344.63 on 2026-10-30 20:00 UTC [S97], the market regime (S&P 500 7,580.07, VIX 19.42 at the 77th percentile, ten-year 4.93%) [S9, S10], and dated regulatory records: the EU DMA fee schedule and EUR500M fine [S77], the D.C. District remedy of 2025-12-05 and the D.C. Circuit appeal No. 26-5023 [S70, S76], the Ninth Circuit contempt of 2025-12-11 and Supreme Court certiorari of 2026-06-30 [S79]. Source register: 147 sources with type, date, confidence and claims, cited by visible [S#] IDs in every section; each section's evidence block records its targeted queries and why each source is decision-grade. Section distinctness: every evidence block carries a plan with the unique decision question, mechanism, comparison set, counter-evidence, best visual, thesis sentence and what makes the section different; sections were checked to remove scaffold labels and repeated card patterns. Evidence matrix: all fourteen sections carry an evidence block with its gate passed (two independent sources, a primary or near-primary source, two numeric facts or a missing-data note, mechanism, comparison, counter-evidence, investor implication, diligence questions). OCR: no client documents were attached and no scanned or slide-heavy material entered the report, so the OCR pipeline and low-confidence OCR rules have no items to apply; no claim in the report rests on OCR text. Company claims: material company-provided claims carry a status label — the 2.5bn installed base, the ~$1bn Gemini licence, the Siri and Private Cloud Compute capability claims and the $1.4tn ecosystem are marked unverified or reported-not-confirmed, and the product section's patent table is marked low confidence. Red-team pass: completed and filed, section 10 written, and five cross-section corrections pushed to their owners. Gaps: seven user data requests filed for records behind logins or paywalls, and the FY2026 10-K is not due until results on 2026-11-02.
profile_requirements.author: Lead Analyst

rows.belief: Replacement demand is mature and price-led: buyers upgrade for battery, camera and now AI, but a 27.6% ASP increase is the live test of willingness to pay.
rows.evidence: Global 2026 smartphone units fall 16.7% to just over 1.0B while value rises 6.3% to $613B and ASP rises 27.6% to $581; Apple's iPhone revenue rose 22.4% in the nine months to 2026-06-27 against that market [S84, S6].
rows.counter_evidence: IDC attributes part of the China strength to purchases pulled forward ahead of Apple's own second-half 2026 price rises and sees China's decline widening to 20% in H2 2026; the sub-$100 segment fell nearly 60% in Q2 2026 [S84, S87].
rows.confidence: medium-high
rows.change: Discounting or a lower-capacity model to hold volume, or a December 2026 quarter that shows unit and mix elasticity.

rows.belief: The moat is real in silicon and the operating system and rented in AI: the intelligence layer protects the franchise without widening it.
rows.evidence: 2nm A20 Pro and in-house C2 modem, 65% of premium phone units, 40.1% product gross margin in the June 2026 quarter (39.9% for the nine months); Siri AI shipped 2026-09-14 as an English beta on a licensed Gemini model confirmed 2026-01-12 [S113, S94, S17, S111].
rows.counter_evidence: The flagship feature runs on a competitor's frontier model and a competitor's TPUs; U.S. patent grants fell 12% to 2,722 in 2025 and no blocking family was verified [S118, S117].
rows.confidence: high on hardware, low on AI
rows.change: Siri exits beta with usage evidence that Apple's integration beats standalone assistants, or a second slip in availability.

rows.belief: 2026 is a price re-pricing cycle, not a growth cycle; the base rate for revenue is mid-single digits.
rows.evidence: Revenue compounded 3.3% a year FY2021-FY2025 ($365.8B to $416.2B) and 5.0% to the last twelve months; the 2026 acceleration is iPhone price/mix and China share gain [S5, S6, S84].
rows.counter_evidence: Foldables could add more than 17M units by 2027 at a $2,550+ ASP, 40% of a $45.7B category, and an AI upgrade cycle could pull demand forward [S84].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: Two consecutive quarters of unit growth in a stable-ASP market.

rows.belief: Distribution scales without new capital: 40% direct and 60% indirect, with India at 25% of assembly and six stores.
rows.evidence: FY2025 net sales of $416,161M at 40/60 direct/indirect; 55M iPhones assembled in India in 2025 against 36M; India sales above $9B [S5, S115].
rows.counter_evidence: Indian assembly and components still cost more than China or Vietnam, and smartphone production subsidies expired on 2026-03-31 [S115].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: Renewal of India's production incentives or evidence of cost parity with China.

rows.belief: The best unit economics in hardware: negative working capital bolted to a 76.3% services annuity.
rows.evidence: TTM revenue $466,823M and gross profit $227,123M; services are 25.8% of revenue but 40.3% of gross profit and cover company R&D 2.1 times; cash conversion cycle of -56.8 days [S6].
rows.counter_evidence: Services fell to 25.2% of revenue from 26.2% as iPhone grew faster, and two services tolls, the App Store commission and the search licence, are being repriced in court [S6, S69, S70].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: Services growth below 10% for two quarters or a structural cut in the App Store take rate.

rows.belief: The bench is deep and insider-built in hardware, operations and finance, and thin and newly reorganised in AI.
rows.evidence: Ternus became CEO on 2026-09-01 with Cook Executive Chair; the CFO (2025-01-01) and COO (2025) were internal promotions; 92% say-on-pay; AI moved under Federighi on 2025-12-01 [S56, S11, S127].
rows.counter_evidence: No filing names an owner of the AI P&L; Srouji was named Chief Hardware Officer on 2026-04-20, which supersedes the December 2025 departure report but leaves key-person concentration with no disclosed successor; the general counsel changed in 2026-03 while the DOJ and DMA cases are live [S133, S141, S132].
rows.confidence: medium
rows.change: A disclosed AI leader with P&L ownership, or the loss of Srouji without a named successor.

rows.belief: Not attractive at this price: the franchise is exceptional, the multiple is not.
rows.evidence: 39.5x trailing and 35.2x forward earnings against a 20.2x peer median, and 32.1x EV/EBIT against 20.5x; the DCF is $277 at 8.5% on a 35% margin, $212 at 9.0% on 33% and $133 at 9.5% on 30%; the base-case rate grid gives $229 at 8.5%/4.0% [S7, S14, S6, S10].
rows.counter_evidence: Forward 35.2x is in line with its own twelve-month forward average of 35.7x, and a 148.8% return on equity has historically held a premium multiple [S7, S6].
rows.confidence: high on the arithmetic, medium on the intrinsic-value gap
rows.change: A de-rating to about $270, or evidence of EPS growth above 12% into FY2027-28.

rows.belief: The exit is the public market and the buyback: liquidity risk is nil, multiple risk is everything.
rows.evidence: 40.41M shares and $13.84B trade daily; no peer is large enough to acquire Apple; the three-year IRR is -3.2% to +4.5% across 27-34x exits on a 1.94% shareholder yield [S7, S14, S6, S97].
rows.counter_evidence: A reversion to the 31.0x four-year mean from 35.2x forward costs 11.9% of the price, about 4.1% a year over three years, and the same daily liquidity is the channel that de-rates in a broad sell-off [S7, S97].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: A sustained multiple above 45x forward, about $440, would be a sale condition rather than a buy signal.

rows.belief: The shares trade above a defensible intrinsic value and above every point of the DCF grid.
rows.evidence: $344.63 on 2026-10-30 against $277 at 8.5% on a 35% margin, $212 at 9.0% on 33% and $133 at 9.5% on 30%; the base-case rate grid gives $229 at 8.5%/4.0% and $193 at 9.5%/4.0%; sum of the parts $177-238; the own-history multiple implies $303 [S7, S6, S17].
rows.counter_evidence: The bull operating case at 8.5% reaches $277, and a 4.93% ten-year Treasury makes a lower discount rate defensible for some buyers, but no grid point on the base operating case reaches the price [S6, S10].
rows.confidence: medium
rows.change: A fall in the ten-year yield toward 4.0%, or long-term growth proven above 6%.

rows.belief: Cash-true but flattered at the margin by tariff refunds and by buybacks.
rows.evidence: Normalised free cash flow covers net income 0.97 times at the centre of a 0.95-0.99x band on capex of 2.2% of revenue, against 0.50x at Microsoft and 0.08x at Alphabet; buybacks added 2.4 points of the 22.4% nine-month EPS growth [S6, S49, S17].
rows.counter_evidence: The 50.1% June-quarter gross margin includes 2 points of one-off tariff refunds worth $0.11 of $2.02 EPS, and FY2025 returned 107% of free cash flow [S17, S5].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: A December-quarter guide below 48% gross margin, a slowdown in repurchases, or a FY2026 10-K that confirms the other-liabilities swing is an unpaid purchase.

rows.belief: Conversion is structurally strong, but the trailing figure overstates the run-rate by a working-capital swing that is partly an Irish tax artefact.
rows.evidence: $136,683M of TTM free cash flow; nine-month operating cash flow rose $35,176M, with other current and non-current liabilities at +$10,016M against -$15,161M a year earlier; the line's clean three-year average is $2,502M, so normalised free cash flow is $122.6-127.3B with $125.1B central, 0.97x conversion, a 2.4-2.5% yield and 40.2x price to free cash flow on the basic market value (40.5x diluted) [S6, S7].
rows.counter_evidence: The normalisation is an analyst estimate, not a filed figure; a $13,531M rise in other non-current liabilities against $13,270M of gross intangibles added is consistent with deferred consideration for intangibles, which puts free cash flow at $123.2B, inside the band at 40.8x on the basic market value [S6].
rows.confidence: medium
rows.change: The FY2026 10-K working-capital and intangible detail due with the 2026-11-02 results.

rows.belief: A fortress: net cash, no debt-funded buyback, manageable maturities.
rows.evidence: Cash and marketable securities of $146,517M against debt of $84,344M, net cash of $62,173M, up from $33,763M while $62,094M of stock was retired; $12.4B of debt due within twelve months [S6, S5].
rows.counter_evidence: $2,604M of unrealised securities losses, $57.0B of purchase obligations and $16.8B of lease commitments [S6, S5].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: A move to net debt, or repurchases funded by new issuance.

rows.belief: Our reading is that the price capitalises the 2026 margin as a base; we expect it to normalise. That is an assumption about the price, not a sourced consensus estimate.
rows.evidence: Guidance of 9-11% revenue growth for the September quarter; consensus iPhone revenue of $252.4B for FY2026 (+20.4%) and $277.4B for FY2027 (+9.9%), with no group-revenue or gross-margin consensus held; our base underwrites 47-48% gross margin, not 50.1% [S71, S72, S6, S17].
rows.counter_evidence: Management beat guidance through FY2026 and launched the iPhone 18 Pro and Duo into the holiday quarter [S17, S113].
rows.confidence: medium
rows.change: A December-quarter guide at or above 49% gross margin with FY2027 memory contracted at fixed prices.

rows.belief: The next twelve months are event-dense and mostly adversarial for the multiple.
rows.evidence: Q4 FY2026 results on 2026-11-02; the DMA fee schedule in force from 2026-10-01; Supreme Court review of link-out fees after certiorari on 2026-06-30; the Google remedy appeal likely in 2027; standard iPhone 18 in spring 2027 [S77, S79, S76, S112].
rows.counter_evidence: There are positive catalysts too: Siri out of beta in five more languages from October 2026 and the spring 2027 iPhone cycle [S113, S112].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: An appellate ruling or settlement that removes the search-payment tail.

rows.belief: Zero today; a first tranche at $270 or below, a second at $245, and the 5% cap only below $225.
rows.evidence: A 9% three-year return needs an entry near $270; $1B is 7.2% of one day's traded value; the realistic bear drawdown is 30% to $241; the full Kelly on the scenario inputs is 337% of the fund, so the 5% cap is a risk-budget limit rather than a sizing output [S7, S6, S97].
rows.counter_evidence: The discipline has been wrong before: the shares returned 27.5% in twelve months, and a valuation-based sale would have missed it [S7, S97].
rows.confidence: medium
rows.change: A de-rating to $270, or a December-quarter guide at or above 49% with memory contracted.

scenarios.driver: The AI upgrade cycle and the foldable Duo extend the iPhone cycle into FY2027-28; services growth stays above 15%; gross margin holds 48% through the memory cycle; the search payment survives at a lower rate.
scenarios.evidence: iPhone revenue rose 22.4% in nine months; iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max list at $1,199 and $1,299; the foldable Duo launched 2026-09-09; IDC expects more than 17M foldable iPhones by 2027 at a $2,550+ ASP [S6, S113, S84].
scenarios.outcome: FY2027 EPS of $10.20 at 35x gives $357, +4% price and about +4.3% total return over twelve months; the DCF at an 8.5% cost of equity on a 35% margin and 14% initial growth is $277; a three-year IRR of up to +9% needs a 34x exit.
scenarios.implication: Own it, but the upside comes from a multiple that stays elevated, not from a margin of safety at entry.

scenarios.driver: Growth fades from 9% to 5%, gross margin normalises to 47-48% as memory costs reset, services grows 12-14%, and the search payment is renegotiated lower.
scenarios.evidence: The DCF is $212 at a 9.0% cost of equity on a 33% margin and 9% initial growth; the 31.0x four-year mean P/E implies $303 on FY2027 EPS of $9.79; revenue compounded 3.3% a year FY2021-25 and 5.0% to the last twelve months [S6, S10, S7, S97].
scenarios.outcome: $284 at 29x FY2027 EPS of $9.79, -18% price and -17.7% total return; the DCF is $212 at 9.0% (33% margin) and $277 at 8.5% (35%); the base-case rate grid gives $229 at 8.5%/4.0%; the three-year IRR is 1.3% at a 31x exit.
scenarios.implication: Do not own at $344.63: the compounding is real but already paid for, and the three-year return is roughly the shareholder yield.

scenarios.driver: Memory costs break the hardware margin below 46%, services growth falls under 8% as the DMA and link-out remedies bite, and the search payment is cut or banned on appeal.
scenarios.evidence: The iPhone 18 Pro bill of materials is up 38% year on year with memory 34% of it; the Ninth Circuit affirmed civil contempt on 2025-12-11; the DOJ cross-appeal seeks a payment ban; losing $20B is 12.9% of EPS [S99, S79, S76, S6].
scenarios.outcome: $241 at 24.6x FY2027 EPS of $9.79, a 30% drawdown; the $133 DCF at a 9.5% cost of equity on 30% margins and 4% growth is the permanent-loss tail; three-year IRR -12% at a 27x exit.
scenarios.implication: The entry price has to price this: even from $270 the three-year return is only 5.0-13.3% across 27-34x exits, so size, not conviction, carries the risk.

assumptions.assumption: Gross margin normalises to 47-48%, not the 50.1% June-quarter print, as tariff refunds lapse and memory costs reset.
assumptions.disproof: A December 2026 quarter guided at or above 49% gross margin with FY2027 memory contracted at fixed prices.
assumptions.impact: -6.0% EPS per 200 basis points of gross margin, and multiple compression on a peak-earnings read [S6, S17].
assumptions.early_warning: The 2026-11-02 guidance and TrendForce bill-of-materials data, where the iPhone 18 Pro BOM is up 38% with memory at 34% of it [S99, S72].

assumptions.assumption: The Google default-search payment survives the D.C. Circuit appeal, renegotiated lower rather than banned.
assumptions.disproof: An appellate ruling banning payments or capping them below the current economics.
assumptions.impact: A ban is -12.9% of EPS and about 15% of FY2025 operating income; a materially lower rate resets the services multiple [S6, S80].
assumptions.early_warning: D.C. Circuit briefing and decision expected in 2027; DOJ and state cross-appeal filed February 2026 [S76, S80].

assumptions.assumption: Services grows 12-14% without relying on hardware mix, and the EU take-rate cut does not accelerate.
assumptions.disproof: Two consecutive quarters of services growth below 10%, or faster migration to external distribution in the EU after 2026-10-01.
assumptions.impact: A 3-point cut in services growth removes roughly a tenth of the sum-of-the-parts value; each $1B of EU commission lost is $0.75B of gross profit [S78].
assumptions.early_warning: The quarterly services line and developer take-up of the 5% Core Technology Commission [S77, S6].

assumptions.assumption: The buyback continues at $80B a year or more with net cash positive, so EPS growth keeps its 2-3 point financial tailwind.
assumptions.disproof: A cut to the authorisation, or repurchases funded by new debt.
assumptions.impact: Buybacks added 2.4 points of the 22.4% nine-month EPS growth; losing that cuts EPS growth to mid-single digits [S6, S17].
assumptions.early_warning: The May 2027 authorisation and the FY2026 10-K cash-flow statement [S5, S6].

assumptions.assumption: The Gemini licence stays an R&D expense and is not repriced per device or per query into services margin.
assumptions.disproof: Renewal terms disclosed that price the model per device or per query.
assumptions.impact: A $1B annual licence is 0.65% of TTM operating income and $0.06 of EPS; per-device pricing at $0.50/$1/$2 across 2.5B devices is $1.25B/$2.5B/$5.0B a year, $0.07/$0.14/$0.28 of EPS [S111, S73].
assumptions.early_warning: Renewal commentary from Apple or Google, and any services margin step-down unexplained by mix [S111].

consensus.consensus: The market pays 39.5x trailing and 35.2x forward earnings. Our reading is that the price capitalises the 2026 margin as a base; that is an assumption about what the price discounts, not a sourced consensus estimate, because no dated consensus gross-margin or group-revenue figure is in the register. The only consensus in the register is iPhone revenue: $252.4B for FY2026 (+20.4%) and $277.4B for FY2027 (+9.9%).
consensus.our_view: Non-consensus on price, not on franchise: the business is a genuine compounder, but the 2026 margin is a peak and no point of the DCF grid reaches $344.63. The evidence supports a watchlist place and an entry near $270, not ownership at the current multiple.
consensus.evidence: The DCF is $277 at 8.5% on a 35% margin, $212 at 9.0% on 33% and $133 at 9.5% on 30%; the base-case rate grid gives $229 at 8.5%/4.0% and $193 at 9.5%/4.0%; the sum of the parts is $177-238; and the June-quarter margin carried 2 points of tariff refunds [S6, S10, S71, S72, S17].
consensus.proof_event: The December-quarter gross-margin guide on 2026-11-02, and the D.C. Circuit decision on the Google payments expected in 2027.

one_question.question: Will the Google default-search payment survive the D.C. Circuit appeal, and at what annual rate?
one_question.why: The payment, put at $20B in 2022 by the trial record, is 18.3% of FY2025 services revenue and about 15% of FY2025 operating income at near-pure margin. A ban or a materially lower rate resets the services multiple that carries most of the valuation, and it moves fair value from the base case toward the bear case regardless of how well the hardware cycle trades.

modules.position_sizing: Watchlist, zero position today. First tranche 0.75-1.0% of the fund at $270 or below, where a 9% three-year return becomes reachable across 27-34x exits; second tranche to 2.5-3.0% at $245; cap the position at 5% below $225. Maximum loss at the cap is 1.5% of the fund on the 30% drawdown; the full Kelly at $270 on the stated inputs is 337% of the fund, so the 5% cap is 1.5% of full Kelly and a risk-budget decision. Sell review above $380 (38.8x the FY2027 build); sell on valuation alone above 45x forward, about $440; sell outright on two quarters of sub-10% services growth, gross margin below 47%, or a structure that removes the search payment.

answers.most_damaging_fact: The survival and size of the Google search payment. The base case assumes it is renegotiated lower, not lost, but a D.C. Circuit ban is -10% to -13% of EPS and, with a services de-rating, -15% to -20% of value (sections 6 and 10, S70, S76, S135). The $20bn figure is a 2022 trial estimate, not a disclosure: if the 2026 payment is 25% larger, the EPS hit is about 16%. The second candidate is the gross-margin assumption: the base case capitalises 47-48%, while TrendForce has DRAM contract prices plus 10-15% in 4Q26 and NAND plus 15-20% with supply tight into 2027 (S136), and a 46% margin puts fair value at $270 at 29x, the entry price itself.
answers.company_only_claims: Five positive claims rest only on Apple material: the 2.5bn active installed base (an earnings-call figure, used for the per-device economics in section 6 and the per-device AI stress in section 10); the Gemini licence at about $1bn a year, which is reported and not confirmed by either company (S111); the Siri capability and Private Cloud Compute privacy claims (Apple Newsroom, S113, S127); the $1.4tn App Store ecosystem (S83); and the 'record installed base' and upgrade-cycle framing. Each is labelled as company-sourced in its section. The $20bn search payment is the opposite case: a litigated estimate, not a company disclosure, and therefore not a company claim.
answers.generic_section: Section 2 (Team) was the thinnest and has been corrected in revision 4: Srouji was named Chief Hardware Officer on 2026-04-20, adding Hardware Engineering to Hardware Technology (S133, confirmed by S141), superseding the December 2025 departure report (S131); what remains is thin disclosure, with no degrees for six of seven executives and AI accountability argued from the absence of disclosure. Section 3 (Technology & Product) is now the weakest: its patent table is mostly 'not verified' and no blocking patent family is established.
answers.unpriced_risk: The AI cost curve. The base case holds a 33% operating margin and treats the Gemini licence as a roughly $1bn R&D expense, but R&D is already up 33% to $34.04bn with no disclosed AI revenue (section 6, S6), and the scenario analysis gives the licence only a low-confidence assumption with no number attached. A per-device or per-query price across the 2.5bn installed base would be several times $1bn and would land in the 76.3% services margin, a 2-4% EPS risk that the $270 entry and the 1.5-2.0% starter size do not adjust for. The same gap covers the xAI suit against Apple over AI distribution, which no section prices.
answers.first_challenge: Why own nothing at 35.2x forward when the franchise compounds at 8-11% and the buyback adds 2.4 points of EPS growth? The answer has to be the exit multiple, not the business: section 12 shows a 1.3% three-year return from $344.63 if the multiple reverts to the 31.0x mean (S97). A partner would immediately challenge the $270 entry as arbitrary, because it is derived from a required 9% return rather than from the franchise: at 29x the scenario base gives $284, so $270 is a 5% discount to the base case, not a margin of safety, and it is above the $241 bear case.
answers.downside_survival: The recommendation survives; the entry price does not. A market 50% smaller takes group revenue down about 35% and EPS to roughly $6, which at 20-25x is $120-150, but $62.2bn of net cash means the company survives and the buyback stops rather than the balance sheet breaking. Revenue 30% lower gives operating income of about $95bn and EPS of $5.4; the bottom of the DCF range is $133 at a 9.5% cost of equity and a 30% margin, and the exit-multiple bear is $241 at 24.6x. Free cash flow 30% lower is $85.8-89.1bn on the $122.6-127.3bn band (central $125.1bn, 0.97x conversion), 56.4-58.6x on the $5,029.6bn market value, which covers the $82.2bn trailing buyback but not $97.9bn of trailing buybacks and dividends; the deferred-consideration case at $123.2bn changes neither, and the $111.5bn reading is withdrawn because the $13,531M non-current build fits inside the $10,016M other-liabilities line once the $4,128M fall in other current liabilities is netted. Net cash absorbs three or more years of the gap. CAC doubling and a six-month financing delay do not apply (no customer acquisition cost; net cash and $12.4bn due within a year), so the analogues are a licence doubling to $2bn, about 1.3% of operating income, and a buyback pause, -2.4 points of EPS growth. Multiple compression from 35.2x forward to 24.6x is -30.1%.
answers.ocr_claims: There are no OCR-derived claims in the report. Every figure in section 10 and in the review comes from an SEC filing, a market-data feed, a named research firm's release or a cited publication, and no client document was read through OCR in this run.
